Huo Congjun stood up, waved his arms, pointed at Ling Ran, and said, “Sitting here means that you can see every movement outside the door, but you’re not at the main position either, meaning you won’t be the target for public criticism.
The windows at the back are also tightly closed.
You won’t be blown by the wind or air conditioner.
They are comfortable to sit in, and you can fight for a long time.
If they are to hold a meeting for a whole day, you won’t easily compromise with them just because of your bodily discomforts.”
Ling Ran observed, agreed, and nodded.
“In addition, the location of the drinking fountain is very important.
If you’re too far away, even when the hot water is ready, you can’t get it.
So, it will be taken away by other people.
You can only drink cold water.
It’s easy to get hungry when you drink cold water, right?
These are all small details which are not usually applicable.
However, if there is a thirty-hour meeting, it is very significant,” Huo Congjun said and laughed out loud.
Ling Ran stared at Huo Congjun, and he was puzzled by what he said.

“Well, if Zuo Cidian is here at this time, he will surely ask, what have you thought of, department director?” Huo Congjun shook his head and said, “I remember that when I took over the Emergency Department, we used the meeting room in the old building.
I kept a hot water bottle with me, and when I came over, I would pour water for the people on my side.
As for the rest, I wouldn’t hand it over to my enemies even if that meant forcing myself to drink it, and those people were so thirsty when they watched me...
When I was young, my kidney functions were really good...”
Ling Ran: Handsome.jpg
Huo Congjun sighed and helped Ling Ran choose a seat.
He concluded, “You like operating theaters, and this is okay.
But in a hospital, meetings can’t be overlooked, especially when they are important meetings like this.
If you really have no idea how to prepare in advance, come earlier and sit in this chair.
Visualize the scene where they become speechless when you scold them.
Your thoughts will start running by then.”
Ling Ran said, “That’s why you got yourself the key to the meeting room?”
Huo Congjun’s high-spirited expression calmed down instantly.
However, who was Huo Congjun?
After a few seconds, he said calmly, “I don’t have to bother others for the key, and it’s convenient for me as well.
Isn’t that good?”
As he spoke, he put his nameplate wherever he wanted and put Ling Ran’s beside his.
The staff members who heard about the meeting came in and stood by the side.
They could only pretend not to see the nameplates.
Although there were rankings and so on when it came to the positions for the participants in meetings like this, no one could say anything when Huo Congjun moved the nameplates himself.
Five minutes later, the meeting room was gradually filled.
Doctors were very busy.
Just got off the plane, about to fly, about to immediately participate in a surgery, and almost finishing a surgery were their usual modes of work.
Doctors who could barely make it for the meeting were already considered very punctual.
Huo Congjun surveyed the doctors who came in coldly.
He had also changed the positions of the nameplates across him, especially the one opposite Huo Congjun.
The nameplate over there clearly stated He Yuanzheng’s name.
When He Yuanzheng himself arrived, Huo Congjun stared at him, and his cold sweat dripped on the ground.
“Most of them are associates.” Huo Congjun watched for a while, and his expression softened.
There was a huge gap between a department director and a chief physician of a hospital.

For a strong department such as the General Surgery Department, if the department director came in person, Huo Congjun really needed to sort out his thoughts and criticize the department director in order.
But if they were just a few associate department directors or associate chief physicians, he did not have to pay too much attention to them.
He could argue however he wanted.
As Huo Congjun thought about this, the smile on his face also gradually became wider, just like a spider plant that was watered too much, so much so that its petals would start to drop to the ground.
He Yuanzheng sat on the opposite side.
He looked at Huo Congjun and Ling Ran.
Annoyance surged up his heart, and his mood was just as sour as pickled vegetables.
“Young He, you don’t have to wear so many layers in the hospital.
I can see the sweat on your forehead,” Huo Congjun chuckled as he said to He Yuanzheng.
It was as if Huo Congjun cared about him.
He Yuanzheng showed a very reluctant smile.
How many clothes was he wearing?
He only wore a scrub beneath his white coat.
If he were to wear less, he would be shirtless.
But the situation in front of him was not that much better than if he were to come to the place shirtless.
As He Yuanzheng was thinking about it, he heard Huo Congjun ask another question.
“What’s your opinion on this case?
Do you support Ling Ran, or do you have another idea?”
Wei Qing, the associate chief physician of the General Surgery Department, hurriedly interrupted Huo Congjun.
In a half-joking tone, he said, “Department Director Huo, the meeting hasn’t started yet.
You can’t have a private mini-meeting here.”
Huo Congjun pursed his lips.
“Isn’t the purpose of this meeting for communication and coordination?
Besides, even if I don’t say it now, I can still say it during the meeting?
And I can say it even after the meeting?
People’s opinions are opinions.
Let others say whatever they want.
What are you afraid of?”

In the order of relationships between the people in the General Surgery Department with the Emergency Department, Wei Qing’s relationship with the Emergency Department was not quite, which meant he was at the lower portion of the order.
On one hand, this was due to each person’s personality.
On the other hand, it was because the intestinal surgeries Wei Qing often did overlapped with a lot of the surgeries the Emergency Department did.
Over the years, there was some discord between Wei Qing and the Emergency Department.
Meanwhile, the General Surgery Department was one of the major departments of Yun Hua Hospital, and because of it, they had a natural need to resist the expansion of the Emergency Department.

If the General Surgery Department were to be divided into factions based on their attitude toward the Emergency Department, Wei Qing could be considered the leader of the anti-Emergency Department in the General Surgery Department.
However, today’s Emergency Medical Center was not vast enough for the General Surgery Department to be divided into factions just yet.
Wei Qing confronted Huo Congjun casually.
“Since we’ve decided to hold a meeting, then we should let the meeting decide this matter.
It’s just an MDT, is there a need for you to ?
Is it there a need for you to make connections in private for it?”
“You’re right.” Huo Congjun agreed with Wei Qing, which was a rare sight to be seen.
He said, “This is Ling Ran’s MDT.”
“Now that everyone is here, let’s start.” The chief physician of the Department of Gastroenterology and Hepatology arrived last.
He looked as if he rushed here.
For him, he did not care about who and how the surgery should be done.
No matter what, it had nothing to do with the Department of Internal Medicine.
“Ling Ran, please introduce the patient’s condition.” Huo Congjun did not intend to exchange pleasantries.
Several surgeons who did not know the intentions of the Emergency Medical Center just smiled as usual.
They only treated this as a regular surgical discussion.
Huo Congjun gave them looks as if he was looking at weaklings, and he thought, ‘You have already lost at the war preparation stage.’

chapters.title: Chapter 907: Taboo
paragraphs: Ling Ran slowly stood up and spoke calmly in front of a group of department directors and associate chief physicians, “The patient is 37 years old... He feels bloated, experiences gastroesophageal reflux, vomiting, but did not pay attention to it... He has received subtotal gastrectomy and lymphadenectomy...”

A multidisciplinary team discussion would have had the related departments sit together as they held a discussion centered around the patient. Each department would take turns in discussing the issue. This discussion mode was started by Mayo Clinic, and the discussion itself consumed a lot of manpower. Mayo Hospital had even purposely built a new multidisciplinary building in order to save as many human resources as possible...
China did not have luxurious facilities like Mayo Clinic, and hence, when they used the multidisciplinary team discussion mode, they could not help but be uncertain during the discussion.

For the regionally best hospitals like Yun Hua Hospital, while they wanted to embrace these futuristic medical treatments, at the same time, they felt that it was a waste of time to make everyone sit together. Therefore, during the discussion, they trembled like a dog whose only purpose was to butter up to its owner, and when they were given a chance to butter up to someone, they would tremble so much that they could not even stand straight.

There were almost no consultation fees given to doctors in the country either. Hence, the application for MDT was always in the negative, since the fee senior doctors from eight departments sitting together for an hour long discussion would usually not even amount to 200 RMB, and that cost did not include the hidden cost of inviting the senior doctors from various departments over for an MDT discussion.
In a hospital like Yun Hua Hospital, usually, MDT discussion would be promoted by the doctors themselves, and it was not a compulsory procedure.

The MDT organized by the Emergency Medical Center this time was not looked forward to by other departments. Everyone was just trying to follow the flow and try to muddle along. When they saw Ling Ran speak, they were too lazy to even open the documents in front of them.

There were only so many things about hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer. The department directors and associate chief physicians in the room were familiar with this disease. It would be very easy for them to say something formal.

After a few minutes, the associate chief physician from the Medical Imaging Department who was the second to speak was even more tired. He said with a moderate tone, “The patient’s CT scans show that the walls of the lesser curvature of the stomach below the cardia has become thicker... The CT scan shows low-density shadows inside the liver. The level of alpha fetoprotein which was used as the combined tumor marker was not high, and the carcinoembryonic antigen can be considered as metastatic nodules, and we can diagnose this as hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer...”

The associate chief physician from the Medical Imaging Department could practically be said to have only said conventional words, and he sat down right after he finished talking. For him, such meetings were really a waste of time. If it were not because of Old Huo, he could not even be bothered to come and report this in the academic conference hall.
The associate chief physician from the Oncology Department coughed and prepared to stand up.
At this moment, Ling Ran said, “Low-density shadows at the liver’s CT scan? Is it okay to stop here?”
The associate chief physician from the Oncology Department was shocked. ‘We’re already starting to criticize each other? Why is Ling Ran the one starting it?’
Even Huo Congjun was shocked. ‘Why is the Medical Imaging Department being criticized first? They are part of our friendly forces...’
Huo Congjun tried to smooth things over and said, “Our Doctor Ling might be a bit too strict sometimes... Ling Ran, our colleagues from the Medical Imaging Department are truly rather busy...”

“Didn’t you see high-density shadows? There are high-density shadows at the borders of the tumor. There is even obvious fluid-fluid level signs here...” Ling Ran shook his head. “The patient has received contrast-enhanced CT scan, and the high-density shadows over here showed that the metastases have eroded the blood vessel, these symptoms must be explained...”
The associate chief physician from the Medical Imaging Department lowered his head and kept searching for information.
He had actually prepared himself mentally before he attended today’s MDT meeting. If he were accidentally criticised by people like Huo Congjun, he would just surrender and take in all the comments.
Since the Medical Imaging Department was just an auxiliary department, normal doctors would not be looking to cause them trouble.
However, what he did not expect was that the first critic was from Ling Ran, and it was directed on technical issues.
‘Technical skills?!
‘I can’t pretend to be ignorant when it comes to technical skills!
‘The Medical Imaging Department also has its own baseline!’
The associate chief physician roared in his heart...

The status of the auxiliary department was already very low in the hospital. Departments like the Medical Imaging Department only obtained their average bonus because of their technical skill. Although it was not to the extent that they thought that their department would not survive without them, in truth, they did have that sort of thought in their heads.
Therefore, challenging the technical skill of the Medical Imaging Department was equivalent to offending them.
The associate chief physician from the Medical Imaging Department quickly flipped the information in the file and was prepared to randomly find some information to oppose Ling Ran first.
Sadly... There was only limited information, and he had not made sufficient preparations.
The associate chief physician from the Medical Imaging Department made his resolve, took out the raw scan, and analyzed it on the spot.

He was a man who was experienced in reading films for over thirty r years. Even though some of the important parts were so blurry that they looked as though they had been pixelated, he could still find the real image through the layers of images!

“The center of the lesion has some dots enhancement. From this, we can tell that it is related to the blood supply of the hepatic artery...” The associate chief physician did not want to keep everyone waiting. He just pretended he could tell something as he analyzed the scan. He said it slowly, as though it was very important.
Ling Ran looked disappointed and said, “Just that?”
“The dot enhancement at the center of the lesion is still quite rare. So, doctors—”

“It’s useless whether you can tell it or not.” Ling Ran interrupted him, completely unconcerned with what the associate chief physician said. He then said, “Now, you should focus on the calcification of the lesion. It’s over here...”
Ling Ran went straight to the side of the table and pointed at the scan in front of the associate chief physician and tapped it lightly twice.
The associate chief physician wore his glasses and put the scan further away from him. It was only at that moment that he saw the small dot Ling Ran mentioned.
“Can you see that now?” Ling Ran asked.
“Yes... multiple calcified fine dots. This is a characteristic of liver metastasis...” the associate chief physician from the Medical Imaging Department said with a softer voice.
It was not because he could not see it before, but because he did not analyze the scan carefully before he came here.

The Medical Imaging Department had to analyze scans for the entire hospital, and they had to analyze countless films every day. The associate chief physician might not be able to touch normal scans on usual days.
However, since he was now at an MDT, it would be unreasonable if he said he did not analyze the scan before he came here.
The associate chief physician was as tame as a kitten when he saw Ling Ran’s serious expression.

He was used to the critics by other experts. However, he was not used to Ling Ran’s criticism as he was still young. As long as he adjusted his mentality and treated Ling Ran as an expert, he would not feel that bad after being criticized.

Surgeons usually had bad tempers, and they always criticized other people. As an auxiliary department, they should already be used to all the scoldings. For those who did not, they could only hide their aggrievance while they pocketed the insults thrown their way.

Now that he was an associate chief physician, he was used to being someone with a low status. At this moment, the associate chief physician smiled shyly and was as carefree as a middle-aged thief recognized by the public in a bus. Everyone thought that he should feel embarrassed, but he was the one who did not think so.
“Let’s continue.” When Huo Congjun saw that the associate chief physician had started to ignore everything around him, he reminded Ling Ran not to waste any time on him.
At the same time, Huo Congjun could not help but use a new perspective to judge Ling Ran.

It was nothing to criticize and scold an associate chief physician from an auxiliary department. Huo Congjun had criticized them countless times. But what was more impressive was that he had actually criticized the department from the angle of technical skills.

In Huo Congjun’s memories, when departments like the Medical Imaging Department talked about their skills, they would usually be very slick about it and not allow anyone to criticize them, remaining as stubborn as hob meat. But now, when he saw them being criticized by Ling Ran in terms of skills, he felt so good.

“Next, Digestive Surgery Department?” Huo Congjun looked to the right. There was a doctor sitting with his back facing the door over there. He was another weakling who did not even know how to choose his seat.
The Digestive Surgery Department also sent out an associate chief physician, and he was as nervous as someone who was partaking in theft for the first time ever in his life.
Everyone could understand what was going on if they were scolded by Old Huo. But if their technical skills were tested, it would be very awkward... or rather, they should feel awkward about it.

The associate chief physician of the Digestive Surgery Department stared at Ling Ran, and he suddenly remembered the gastrectomies Ling Ran performed. He felt his stomach clenching down on itself tightly, and could not help but complain in his heart.’Since Ling Ran’s gastrectomy skill is better than mine, what is the point of me coming for today’s meeting? Why didn’t I make full preparation before coming here?’
“Associate Chief Physician Ding?” Ling Ran did not want to waste time, so he urged him to speak.

“Why not... we have Department Director He from the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery speak first...?” Associate Chief Physician Ding from the Digestive Surgery Department was like an elementary school kid who had not memorized his text and had someone else take the bullet for him.

He Yuanzheng was already very anxious. He immediately jumped when he heard this, as though the fat on his butt had just taken a cattle prod, and he said, “Why should I speak first? This is a patient from the General Surgery Department, right? Let the General Surgery Department speak first.”

Before the meeting, Wei Qing had been unyielding, but when he looked at Ling Ran now, he remembered the way Ling Ran performed his surgeries, and he could not help but say, “This is not a patient from the General Surgery Department...”

chapters.title: Chapter 908: Next
paragraphs: Huo Congjun gave Wei Qing a scrutinizing look, as if he was looking at a supreme grade steak and was wondering whether he wanted it well-done, medium raw, or raw, to the point that he could tear it off with his teeth.
The temperature in the room increased slightly. That was because the staff had increased the temperature of the air conditioner a little according to Huo Congjun’s personal request.
“Old Ding, it’s your turn. Just say what you want to say.” Wei Qing could feel the pressure and immediately said that.

The Digestive Surgery Department was also a department separated from the General Surgery Department. As an associate chief physician of the General Surgery Department, Wei Qing felt that he was better than an associate chief physician of the Digestive Surgery Department.

Associate Chief Physician Ding of the Digestive Surgery Department pursed his lips bitterly and felt embarrassed to pass the baton to others again. He coughed and drank some water before he looked at the report in his hands. He let it go and decided to switch directions and said, “From the perspective of the Digestive Surgery Department, surgery is already a kind of palliative care for patients with hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer. Right now, the patient’s body condition is not quite ideal for surgery, and we think that it is pointless to carry out the surgery. We suggest a chemotherapy plan for this patient. Hmm... let’s see if single drug chemotherapy using capecitabine can help to eliminate the disease...”

According to the previous plan designed by the Digestive Surgery Department, they still supported the idea of surgery. Since they were all from the Surgery Department, resection would always be their first choice. If it were not possible to cut it or they did not have the skill to do so, they would only think about other methods of interference or use drugs.

However, if Associate Chief Physician Ding looked at the original plan right now, he felt that he would be criticized by Ling Ran until he died. So, he decided to go against the flow instead. At least, he would then be criticized to death for his ideals.
Ling Ran listened carefully to the comments by Associate Chief Physician Ding, and just as expected, he was stunned.

Associate Chief Physician Ding showed a smile when his goal was achieved. When he smiled, he opened his mouth slightly and showed that his lips were a light pink, just like a medium raw steak, and he thought. ‘If you want to go against surgeons, you’ll have to use the methods used by internists against surgeons. If you discuss surgery plans with a surgeon like Ling Ran and your skills aren’t as good as his, you might end up destroyed. Besides, I wouldn’t dare to mention plans that are too difficult, or else I’ll be asked to make a practical demonstration. And the plan which I’m quite adept with can do nothing for a surgery at this level.’

The doctors from other departments also looked enlightened. All doctors in the room were cut from the same cloth, and they could immediately see through the trick used by Associate Chief Physician Ding.
Some of them even stared at Ling Ran with amused expressions. They wanted to see how he would handle this.
Ling Ran thought for a while.
He had done many researches since he went back for Young Dai’s medical case.

Ling Ran should be the most suitable surgeon to perform surgical resection for hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer, since he knew subtotal gastrectomy and had Perfect Level Hepatectomy. However, there would always be better paths to be taken or unique solutions for each specific patient.

If diseases were treated as exam questions, then if the patient’s symptoms were more commonly seen, that also meant that the doctors would know more prerequisite conditions as to whether the patient could receive surgery, and they could also provide even more solutions to treat the patient. The success rate of the answers they provided would also be higher. Most of the time, if they followed the prescribed order in providing treatment for the patient, the results they obtained would be the best for the patient.

Yet, for patients like Young Dai, it would be very unlikely to obtain the best possible treatment outcome, because not only did the patient not provide a lot of prerequisite conditions for him to receive surgery, he also gave a lot of limitations.
Ling Ran had actually thought about Associate Chief Physician Ding’s reply before. Although he did not go into details about it, he did indeed consider things from this aspect.

“Even palliative care means a lot for the patient.” Ling Ran stopped for a while and said, “It’s understandable that all of you think that it’s impossible to perform the surgery. Okay. Let’s end our discussion of the topic here.”

“Old He, go on.” The director of the Oncology Department directly mentioned He Yuanzheng’s name.

After all, He Yuanzheng was not a doctor originally from Yun Hua Hospital. His foundation was not stable, and he did not have a lot of skills. Hence, it was only par for the course that he would soon reach his end.

He Yuanzheng made his resolve, straightened his neck, gritted his teeth, raised his head, frowned, opened his eyes wide, and said with a loud voice, “Doctor Ling, why don’t you tell us what you plan to do?”

chapters.title: Chapter 909: Surge of Emotions
paragraphs: Huo Congjun had a tense face as he left the meeting room.
He was afraid that if he laughed, it would make it too awkward for the other doctors, and thus, affect subsequent collaborations between them.
But after returning to the Emergency Medical Center, Huo Congjun could not help but burst out laughing.

“Ling Ran, did you see the last look on Wei Qing, the one from the General Department? It’s so amusing.” Huo Congjun shook his head and laughed, his white teeth reflected the light from the ceiling lights, but the light reflected was faint.
Ling Ran gave Department Director Huo a rather general smile, which both soothed his mood and allowed the dialogue to continue.

“The General Surgery Department has always been conservative. This time, you could be said to have punched them in the gut.” Huo Congjun recalled the scene in the meeting room and could not help but chuckle cheerfully.

After He Yuanzheng had given up, the other people from the General Surgery Department such as Wei Qing and the others, had also given up on trying to speak, which was equivalent to them surrendering their rights over the patient with both hands.

If a person without any ulterior motives whatsoever said something to a person, a person with a different intention would decipher his or her words differently, which meant that the listener will be the one definitely suffering a setback.
Besides, Ling Ran also had absolute power and authority in hepatectomy.

In fact, doctors and even researchers would usually avoid this kind of situation. Regardless of at what scale the meeting was held, as long as it was a professional topic, it was inevitable that the voice of professionals would be better than that of non-professionals. The weightage would be even more skewed to the professionals when it came to a patient’s life and death. If there was no absolute need, no one would want to have any confrontation.

Take, for example, the operation on a stomach cancer with a metastasis from the liver. Forget about everything else, because Ling Ran might truly be the only person in the meeting room just now who could handle the operation on his own. This point itself caused Wei Qing and the others to have no way of competing against Ling Ran.

This was also the normal life in a hospital: a person had to stay quiet if his skill was not as good as another. The more formal the occasion, the more everyone did not care about the wails of a defeated dog and its inner struggles, pain, along with its helpless consideration of its dreams and pursuits...

Surgical abilities were the most important benchmark for surgeons. Only when everyone was on the same level would there be room for fair discussion of skills. Otherwise, it was only natural that those who had stronger skills would bully those who were weaker.
Huo Congjun deeply enjoyed the nature of such unfairness.
“Maybe, one day, we’ll just open a gastrointestinal clinic.” This sudden sentence from Huo Congjun’s mouth was not just a spontaneous idea that popped up in his mind.

Emergency Departments opening gastrointestinal clinics were actually a common sight. Compared with specialist outpatient clinics, it mainly dealt with common intestinal diseases such as acute diarrhea. It did not mean much for the General Surgery Department, but it was an important part of Huo Congjun’s plan to create a big emergency department.
If not for the strong capabilities of Yun Hua Hospital’s General Department, he would have opened a gastrointestinal clinic a long time ago.
Ling Ran furrowed his eyebrows and said, “I don’t really have time to perform surgeries on intestines for the time being.”

Huo Congjun chuckled softly. “It’s mainly things like infusion and fluid replacement. You can just continue doing your hepatectomy. Right, for the patient’s side, let Zuo Cidian explain and make things clear to him. We’ll need at least two copies of documents such as informed consent forms. The patient as well as the family members must sign them. It would be best to get a few of his immediate family members to sign the papers.”
“There seems to be no one else in the patient’s family.” Ling Ran paused for a moment and thought about it before he said, “The couple should be the only ones in the family.”
“Oh, I remember now. They eloped, right? Was it because the woman’s parents disapproved of their relationship? What about the man’s parents?”
“They all died,” Ling Ran answered.

“Oh,” Huo Congjun said, and stopped pursuing the matter. He then said, “Having relatively simple family relationships is good as well. That means that we don’t have to be too bothered. Then... we still need to take more photos when you’re performing the surgery. How about this? I will find someone to record you, and it can be used as material in the future. It would be convenient for you to use it to give lectures for the housemen and interns, and it’ll also be easy for you when you write articles.”
“Alright.” Ling Ran agreed.

In the world’s top hospitals such as Mayo Clinic, photographers were directly attached to the operating theater and were called surgical photographers. That was because the surgeries that were performed in Mayo Clinic could mostly be used to show off to the world.
Of course, it was also because the cost of cameras nowadays was really low now.
“Well... then that’s settled. If there is anything else, let’s talk about it later, you’ll just need to prepare for the surgery,” Huo Congjun said and started to laugh again.

He actually had the intention to promote this case. The number of people in China performing stomach metastasis from liver cancer had only just begun increasing over the recent years. As Yun Hua hospital had not carried out a lot of such cases themselves, it was even rarer to see such cases being carried out in Changxi Province. If the surgery was successful, with a little bit of work, it would be good promotional material.

However, it was not necessary to say these things to Ling Ran. Instead of just increasing the pressure on Ling Ran, Department Director Huo was more willing to laugh at the details of the previous meeting.
He thought so and did the same. His row of white teeth had never stopped shining after entering the Emergency Medical Center.

The resident doctor who looked so ordinary that no one could remember his name watched Huo Congjun’s terrifying laughter and could not help but worry, “Is there a major accident that led to a large number of casualties today?”
“Why do you say so?” Doctor Zhou had his hands placed behind his back. He watched his resident doctor work and asked casually.
“I think Director Huo’s smile is abnormal. He’s smiling too happily.”
Doctor Zhou looked up and saw only Huo Congjun’s back. He could not help but smile, “Old Huo is not Hanba . It’s not like if he smiled, a serious injury or death would occur.”
“Doctor Zhou, you better remember those words.” The resident doctor quickly emphasized.

Doctor Zhou pouted. “And what words would those be? Just do your work. Look at you. You’re a resident doctor, and you have been one for so many years, but you’re still performing sutures for me. Look at Ling Ran, he has already started to perform combined resections of the liver and pancreas.”
The resident doctor who looked so ordinary that no one could remember his name looked directly at Doctor Zhou. “Are you serious?”

“A man who does not work hard in his youth will end up grieving when he grows old. You have to motivate yourself at all times. Alright, I will leave it to you to deal with it. Write the case report in a while, and be quick to read the test report as well. There’s also a woman who has just been hospitalized so that she can be under observation. Remember to perform an electrocardiogram scan for her, and change the medicine of the old man we checked earlier in the morning... “Doctor Zhou walked as he spoke. The more he talked, the more somber he sounded, and the farther he went...

It was visitation hours for the ICU right now. Wang Chuanwen, Wang Chuanming, and Wang Chuanmao sat in the waiting room politely and let their youngest brother pay his respect and visit Wang Chuanli, who was still confined to his bed.
When Ling Ran arrived, Wang Chuanwen, Wang Chuanming, and Wang Chuanmao quickly got up. They looked as if they wanted to give him a small but grand welcome.
“Doctor Ling, are you doing ward rounds?” Wang Chuanwen asked a superfluous question in a respectful manner.
Ling Ran acknowledged Wang Chuanwen and said, “Your brother’s condition is stable. If he lasts for a few more days, he should be able to be transferred to a general ward. Don’t worry.”

Ling Ran behaved like many other surgeons in this case. The more critical the patient’s condition, the longer he stayed in the ward, and the better Ling Ran’s attitude became, just like other surgeons. He would also speak more, and the memories relevant to the patient also became clearer.
A few of Wang Chuanli’s organs were removed, and he was naturally one of his more critically ill patients. Ling Ran obviously had a deep impression about him.
Wang Chuanwen quickly thanked him, then hesitated for a few seconds, and said, “I heard that you’re going to perform an operation on the young man who eloped and is inside the operating theater?”

“I’m intending to.” Ling Ran did not care why he asked, he just answered the question when it was directed at him, but he said it more briefly. Wang Chuanwen was one of Wang Chuanli’s family members, but he was not related to Young Dai.

However, Wang Chuanwen heaved a long sigh and nodded again and before he said, “That’ll be alright then, I believe that if you are the one performing the surgery, the young couple will not have to suffer so much.”
Ling Ran froze and looked at Wang Chuanwen, as he did not understand why he said those words.

“The young couple is very pitiful. The girl actually eloped with her husband, and her family disowned her. She can only depend on her husband. They could have originally lived an ordinary, steady life, but now that her husband is diagnosed with cancer...” Having said this, Wang Chuanwen smiled helplessly, looked up, and said, “Isn’t that how life is? I guess, if the girl’s parents see their daughter like this, they will regret their decision.”
Ling Ran nodded and did not say much.

“I wish your surgery to be a successful one.” Wang Chuanwen just wanted to express his emotions. The days of looking after his younger brother in the ICU were enough for him to feel depressed, and now he cannot help but want to say a thing or two.
Ling Ran still nodded just a little, stood in front of the door for a little while before he replied, “Sure.”
The three brothers of the Wang family felt an inexplicable surge of emotions when they stood behind Ling Ran.

“The young couple is very pitiful.
The girl actually eloped with her husband, and her family disowned her.
She can only depend on her husband.

They could have originally lived an ordinary, steady life, but now that her husband is diagnosed with cancer...” Having said this, Wang Chuanwen smiled helplessly, looked up, and said, “Isn’t that how life is?
I guess, if the girl’s parents see their daughter like this, they will regret their decision.”
Ling Ran nodded and did not say much.
“I wish your surgery to be a successful one.” Wang Chuanwen just wanted to express his emotions.
The days of looking after his younger brother in the ICU were enough for him to feel depressed, and now he cannot help but want to say a thing or two.
Ling Ran still nodded just a little, stood in front of the door for a little while before he replied, “Sure.”
The three brothers of the Wang family felt an inexplicable surge of emotions when they stood behind Ling Ran.

chapters.title: Chapter 910: The Best
paragraphs: Young Dai was still in a semi-comatose state. His wife, Young Feng, fetched a pot of hot water and carefully wiped his feet and hands.
From time to time, she looked at her husband and seemed to want to say something, but Young Dai never opened his eyes.
“You should sit and rest for a while.” A nurse came to Young Feng and said softly. Then, she felt her throat itch, and she coughed.
The technique of speaking softly was rare for ICU nurses.
Being crude, fierce, and having a bad temper were the true traits of ICU nurses, but they truly sympathized with Young Feng, which was why even the nurses subconsciously lowered their voices.

“Thank you.” Young Feng reluctantly stood up, knowing that the nurse was very being very nice, forced herself to smile, and whispered, “When Young Dai first entered the ICU, I hoped that he can get well sooner and go home earlier... but in the end, every time, I have to go home by myself...”

“Isn’t the surgery already scheduled? You might be able to both go back after the surgery is over and stay for a few days over here.” The nurse didn’t know how to console her. Some of the patients in the ICU returned happily, but there were more of them who left in silence.
If they had to say that they were already used to this sight, then yes, they had already indeed become accustomed to it.
However, the nurses who were also women could not help but empathize with family members like Young Feng.

She gave up on a good family, courageously eloped with her lover, established her own small family, and worked hard to finally establish a career. Then, the news of her husband’s stomach cancer came...
The nurses looked at Young Feng and felt their hearts go out for her.

“It’s better if her husband found another lover instead. At least she could ask him to divorce her without taking anything. Then, she gets the money.” The old nurse sat at the nurse’s desk, looked at Young Feng’s back from a distance, and blabbered a little.
“Then I would rather my husband be ill and die,” the young nurse beside her muttered, dissatisfied with the plot set by the old nurse.
“It’s cleaner if he died in a car crash. Not only would she get all the money, she’ll be compensated on top of it.” A senior nurse sighed and seemed to have thoroughly researched this matter.
“Can’t you think of something good instead?” Doctor Yan, the ICU’s attending physician, could not bear to listen further.

The young nurse said half-jokingly, “It’s best if he’s not ill, but we wouldn’t see those cases over here. In all honesty, I’ll just be thankful that he’s cured. I think the couple still has a bit of savings. I heard that they run a wholesale business. Sigh, hopefully, they won’t end up with no money in their pockets, and the wife even loses her husband. They’re both business people, they’ll need money for the turnover of capital.”
Doctor Yan smiled, not knowing what was going on. “It’s not that easy to be cured.”
As he was talking, Doctor Yan’s eyes fell on Ling Ran, who had just entered.
Ling Ran had just taken a hot bath and dried his hair. His hair was slightly fluffy, and he looked like a young lion who just woke up.
Doctor Yan was so excited that all his fatigue was gone.
When he faced Ling Ran now, he did not dare to show any signs of inattentiveness. He cleared his throat quickly and came forward to say, “Doctor Ling, you’re here for a ward round again?”

“Yes. How’s Young Dai’s situation?” Ling Ran directly called the patient’s name but did not call the bed number. That was because the surgery for stomach metastasis from liver cancer was truly a major surgery worth remembering.
Young Feng, who heard movement, stood up and looked at Ling Ran in panic.
To her, every doctor’s arrival was worrying.
Doctor Yan glanced at her and said, “He’s in a stable situation. A CT scan was performed this morning. The area has increased slightly.”
“Let me see.” Ling Ran craned his neck forward and looked at the screen in front of him without touching anything.
A nurse immediately pulled out Young Dai’s CT scan and then adjusted it to a convenient angle for Ling Ran.
“The pupil sign is very obvious.” Ling Ran looked at the plain film with a solemn expression.

Tumors with liver metastases, due to their strong metabolism and relatively insufficient blood supply, would have symptoms of necrosis at an early stage. A large number of tumor cells would starve to death at the center of the lesion, resulting in a low-density shadow in the center of the lesion.

Since the tumor cells at the center died, there would thus be different degrees of grayness reflected on the CT scan, and a tumor with a larger area would have different gray levels from normal cells, such tumors were called pupil signs when seen in CT scans because the lesion looked like a pupil.
If the area of central necrosis was so large that the area of necrosis was larger than the tumor, the CT film would show a doughnut sign.
Those in between were called the bullseye sign.
Young Dai’s liver metastasis was not very extensive, which was also the basis for his surgery being approved, but the tumor had obviously not stopped growing...
“He received chemotherapy once?” Ling Ran asked in a whisper.
“Yes.”

“See if you can make further adjustments, and we’ll try to start the surgery tomorrow.” Ling Ran did not immediately request for a surgery. For cases of stomach cancer with liver metastasis, a certain degree of chemotherapy must first be performed, and then the effect of the surgery will be better.

Doctor Yan also went through the related articles over the past few days and nodded in approval. He glanced at Young Feng and said to Ling Ran, “Doctor Ling, the patient’s family is just ahead. Would you like to say something to them?
“Say what?” Ling Ran asked straightforwardly and simply.
Doctor Yan froze and said, “Preoperative discussion?”
“Zuo Cidian has already talked to her.” Ling Ran paused and said, “The family chose to do surgery to extend his survival time, right?”
“Certainly.” Doctor Yan sighed and understood Ling Ran what he meant.

Combined radical liver and stomach surgery was said to be radical, but it was unlikely that the person could be completely cured. Only very few people have miraculously survived longer than expected, and almost none of the ordinary patients could survive through the three-year survival period even after receiving the surgery; there was not even a need to record the statistics for a five-year survival rate.

However, compared with waiting for death in the ICU, or even dying instantly in coma, there was a certain probability of survival for two years and a higher probability of survival for one year, which was the significance of this surgery. It is up to the patient and his family to decide whether to spend the money and energy on this surgery, along with enduring the pain that came from the treatment.
Doctor Yan could not help looking at Young Feng and Young Dai, and he said, “For them, even if they have only another one year to stay with each other, they would be happy.”

Ling Ran also looked over for a while as well before he continued his rounds. The patients who had undergone hepatectomy a few days ago had not yet been discharged from the hospital. For these patients, a hepatectomy operation was also a life-threatening experience, and they did not know what the future would hold for them.
*Beep Beep*
The monitor of a hospital bed sounded unexpectedly.
Ling Ran took a side step and strode over to the bed. He took a look and said, “ST-elevation, myocardial infarction, inform the Cardiology Department.”
As he spoke, Ling Ran started to perform external chest compressions.

“Doctor Ling, you’re performing CPR by himself?” It was the younger brother, Wang Chuanwen’s time to come and visit Wang Chuanli at this time. He then saw that Ling Ran was already performing compressions with all his strength.

The requirements for external chest compressions were extremely high when it came to performing effective CPRs, and in-hospital resuscitation was also the most efficient out of all forms of resuscitation, hence, Ling Ran naturally went and performed external chest compressions, trusting no one else but himself to give the patient the highest chance to survive.
The young nurse next to him was also familiar with CPR. She placed both her hands under her chin. “Because Doctor Ling’s CPR is the best.”
“The most effective.” Another nurse who was silently changing the patient’s medication said in favor. Her eyes were not quite focused.
“He’s really good.” The senior nurse who knew Wang Chuanwen, intentionally stressed on this point.
Wang Chuanwen smiled and seemed to be deep in thought.

chapters.title: Chapter 911: Fresh
paragraphs: “Doctor Ling, let’s take a rest.” Doctor Yan’s eyes were lifeless, and he looked as tired as a doctor from the Ling Treatment Group.
Ling Ran, who had just resuscitated a patient, raised his head and saw that the mission column on the system’s interface had changed.
[Mission: Treat the Wounded and Sick- New (New)]
[Mission Details: Resuscitate 10 patients in the ICU (10/10) and complete combined stomach and liver radical surgery]
[Mission Reward: Cardiac Trauma Repair (Master Level) and a bottle of Energy Serum]

Just like that, he completed his initial mission to resuscitate 10 patients in the ICU. Ling Ran nodded internally and glanced at the clock. He then said to Attending Physician Yan who could not even stand up straight anymore, “I’m going to leave and rest now. It’s not time for you to get off work yet, is it?”
“It’s not time yet?” Doctor Yan froze for a moment and sighed. “Time is passing really slowly today.”
There were only first-string doctors and second-string doctors in Yun Hua Hospital’s ICU.

All the moderately experienced doctors including attending physicians and junior doctors were first-string doctors, and they had to be on shift in the ICU whether it was day or night. They barely got any rest. Compared to the attending physicians in the Emergency Department where doctors were divided into first-string, second-string, and third-string doctors, the attending physicians in the ICU had a harder time.
There was no helping it. The situation was different in the ICU compared to the Emergency Department, and there had to be experienced doctors in the ICU at all times.
However, resuscitating patients like this together with Ling Ran was a little over the boundaries of Doctor Yan’s experience.
Doctor Yan massaged his aching arms. He muttered the same thing over and over again today, “We’ve performed way too many CPRs today, and they’re way too long.”

“But we managed to save those patients.” Ling Ran massaged his shoulders too. He then grabbed a bottle of alcohol-based hand sanitizer and rubbed his hands while he was at it. He said to Doctor Yan, “Why don’t I give you a massage?”
Doctor Yan froze for a moment and nodded. The moment Ling Ran placed his hands on Doctor Yan’s neck, the latter finally realized what Ling Ran meant.
“Doctor Ling, you’ve worked hard too. This is too embarrassing... Mmm...” Doctor Yan only resisted for a short while before closing his eyes.
‘This is way too comfortable.
‘How can it be this comfortable?’
“Do doctors in the Emergency Department get treated like this every day?” Doctor Yan knew that this was impossible, but he could not help but feel jealous.
Ling Ran smiled nonchalantly. “If they’ve performed a major surgery or done something rather tiring such as prolonged CPR, I’ll give them a massage.”
Doctor Yan trembled violently when he heard the phrase “prolonged CPR”, and he became wide awake.
Why was he tremendously tired even though it was not time to get off work yet? It was because Ling Ran insisted on performing prolonged CPR.

Aside from that, Ling Ran was extremely strict when it came to the quality of the chest compression performed during prolonged CPR. It was almost to the point that he was only kind of satisfied with Doctor Yan’s performance, who was an attending physician.
When he thought about how tiring things were for the past few hours, Doctor Yan suddenly felt that it was not really worth it to work so much just for a massage...
He could only feel fortunate that Ling Ran did not work in the ICU.

When he thought of this, Doctor Yan realized something else. He turned to look at Ling Ran and said in a solemn tone, “Doctor Ling, you should really go back and rest. You belong to the Emergency Department, after all. You’ve been in the ICU for too long.”

Even though it felt excellent to have Ling Ran help out while he was on shift, if Ling Ran felt entitled to help out at the ICU whenever he wanted to, it would be too dangerous... Especially since he liked performing prolonged CPR so much...

“Alright. I’ll go and rest, then.” Ling Ran did not give it much thought, though. The ICU did not only consist of patients from the Emergency Department. Instead, it was responsible for patients who were sent over from all the departments in the hospital. It might be convenient for the Emergency Department to take over the ICU, but patients from other departments needed treatment and care too. Ling Ran was not so powerful that he could control all the departments in the hospital yet, so he did not plan to open this closet full of skeletons.

Truth be told, to ensure that he could complete the system’s mission, Ling Ran had already drunk a bottle of Energy Serum today. He could not help but think about how this mission only rewarded him with Cardiac Trauma Repair (Master Level) and a bottle of Energy Serum. Since he used up one bottle of Energy Serum just to complete the mission, it was almost a losing deal.
It was not like Ling Ran could waste all of his time in the ICU and forget about his main duty, anyway.
Doctor Yan could not care less about what Ling Ran was thinking about. He quickly sent Ling Ran away.
He had been working in the ICU for around ten years, but with Ling Ran’s presence, today could be said to be the toughest day in his career.

Even if he were to disregard other things, the resuscitating of patients definitely required CPR, and 30 minutes was usually the maximum time doctors would spend on CPR. Even if they were to do it for a full 30 minutes, for the last 20 minutes, they would usually perform as horribly as an intern.

In Chinese hospitals, many of the times, even if there was already no hope for the patients, the patients’ family members liked it when the doctors looked like they were trying their best to save the patients. Hospitals also upheld the policy that the dead were kings, so the hospitals had no choice but to fulfill the patients’ family members’ desire to try and resurrect the dead.

Of course, Ling Ran did not ask for the doctors in the ICU to perform prolonged CPR on every single patient. However, for the past ten hours, he had ordered them to perform pretty prolonged CPR on two patients, and throughout the duration of the resuscitation, he wanted every single chest compression to be perfect. Doctor Yan had never experienced anything like this.
But the two patients ended up surviving courtesy of Ling Ran.
So, there was nothing that he could say about it.
In the field of medicine, theories and speculations were pointless. Even the most flawless theories had to give way to reality.

If a doctor had a way to save patients from the brink of death every single time, there was no point for an attending physician in the ICU to complain of fatigue. He would have no choice but to do as that doctor said.
Doctor Yan did have the intention to learn prolonged CPR from Ling Ran. But before he mastered the craft, he really did not want to work together with Ling Ran again.
After all, people needed to live their lives, did they not?
Doctors needed to live their lives too!
Ling Ran walked out of the ICU in a natural manner. He then took a shower and changed into a full set of clothes.
This was the third set of clothes he was changing into today.
He encountered a patient who kept vomiting and one who was suffering from major hemorrhage just now, and he was forced to scrub himself clean after he was done resuscitating them.
Even now, there were quite a lot of germs and stains on Ling Ran’s body.
Ling Ran was thinking about how his new underpants would not be put to good use after he went home. Considering the cost-effectiveness ratio, he took out a pair of 59 RMB underpants and put it on.
Ever since he started performing freelance surgery, the first thing he upgraded was his wardrobe. This 59 RMB pair of underpants was his cheapest underpants.
He felt light and comfortable after changing into the pair of clean 59 RMB underpants. And after putting on his large white coat, Ling Ran looked even more fresh and handsome.

He returned to his office to retrieve his car keys and other things. He was about to go downstairs when Lu Wenbin ran over with a mysterious expression on his face. Lu Wenbin looked pleased with himself as he said, “Doctor Ling, I have a patient with four severed fingers. Do you want to operate on him?”
Ling Ran hesitated for a few seconds. He lowered his head to look at his crotch that had his pair of 59 RMB underpants and furrowed his eyebrows a little.
“If you’re busy, I’ll do it together with Chief Physician Wang,” Lu Wenbin quickly added.
“I’ll do it.” Ling Ran immediately made a decision. He then added, “Go ahead to the operating theater first. I’ll join you after I shower.”

After all, people needed to live their lives, did they not?
Doctors needed to live their lives too!
Ling Ran walked out of the ICU in a natural manner.
He then took a shower and changed into a full set of clothes.
This was the third set of clothes he was changing into today.
He encountered a patient who kept vomiting and one who was suffering from major hemorrhage just now, and he was forced to scrub himself clean after he was done resuscitating them.
Even now, there were quite a lot of germs and stains on Ling Ran’s body.
Ling Ran was thinking about how his new underpants would not be put to good use after he went home.
Considering the cost-effectiveness ratio, he took out a pair of 59 RMB underpants and put it on.
Ever since he started performing freelance surgery, the first thing he upgraded was his wardrobe.
This 59 RMB pair of underpants was his cheapest underpants.
He felt light and comfortable after changing into the pair of clean 59 RMB underpants.
And after putting on his large white coat, Ling Ran looked even more fresh and handsome.
He returned to his office to retrieve his car keys and other things.
He was about to go downstairs when Lu Wenbin ran over with a mysterious expression on his face.
Lu Wenbin looked pleased with himself as he said, “Doctor Ling, I have a patient with four severed fingers.
Do you want to operate on him?”
Ling Ran hesitated for a few seconds.
He lowered his head to look at his crotch that had his pair of 59 RMB underpants and furrowed his eyebrows a little.
“If you’re busy, I’ll do it together with Chief Physician Wang,” Lu Wenbin quickly added.
“I’ll do it.” Ling Ran immediately made a decision.
He then added, “Go ahead to the operating theater first.
I’ll join you after I shower.”

chapters.title: Chapter 912: How He Was Treated at Home
paragraphs: Even though the patient had four severed fingers, the entire surgery only took Ling Ran three hours and a pair of 168 RMB underpants.

Compared with hepatectomy and other abdominal surgeries, hand surgeries were a lot more straightforward, and the moment the surgery ended, the doctor would have an idea about the success rate of the surgery. It was different from hepatectomy, where the patients might face all kinds of danger. It was to the point that even three days after surgery, there was still a high chance that the patient might die.

Meanwhile, Lu Wenbin was rather excited. Patients with four severed fingers were pretty rare. Aside from this, Ling Ran was giving Lu Wenbin a lot of opportunities to show his skills. And this made him feel even better than when he was operating on a patient alone.

“As expected, it’s more fun to operate on patients with a few people compared to doing it alone.” After Ling Ran was done showering again, Lu Wenbin fished out a piping hot pork trotter from a pot of braised soup. He placed it on a beautiful porcelain plate, passed it to Ling Ran and said with a smile, “Give this pork trotter a try. It’s from a carefully selected giant pig.”
“Carefully selected giant pig?”

“You know how pigs are hard to come by nowadays, and even pork trotters have become smaller. All the pigs in slaughterhouses are only around 170 or 180 pounds, and how big can their hooves get? Just compare the shoe size of a 170-pound person with that of a 300-pound person. Everyone wants to eat big pork trotters, don’t you think so? So I specially picked out the hooves of gigantic pigs and started this brand called ‘carefully selected giant pigs’. Each pork trotter is 10 RMB more expensive compared to normal ones,” Lu Wenbin explained with a smile. He never earned much from his pork trotters business, but this sudden idea had brought him so much money that he brought a Mercedes-Benz.

Ling Ran did not care about pigs. He ate a few pork trotters with his hands to fill his belly. He then rose and said, “I’m going back to sleep. If you have more pork trotters, do send some to the nurses and doctors in the ICU.”

He had worked in the ICU for only one day, but Ling Ran received a lot of help from the nurses there. Those nurses have given him a lot of fruits and milk too. Since the pork trotters Lu Wenbin gave him today were even more delicious than the usual ones, he immediately decided to let the medical staff members in the ICU have some.
Lu Wenbin felt honored, and he quickly said, “No problem. I’ll definitely choose the best ones and send them there.”
“Just send an invoice to me after you send the pork trotters over.” Ling Ran waved and headed to the elevator.

At this moment, Zuo Cidian who was already so tired that he could barely open his eyes said in a strained voice, “Doctor Ling, do send some to the patients’ family members who are waiting outside the ICU too.”
“Okay, sure thing.” Ling Ran did not think much about it, and he immediately agreed to it due to his trust in Zuo Cidian.
Lu Wenbin watched as Ling Ran entered the elevator before he looked suspiciously at Zuo Cidian. “Old Zuo, are you trying to make me our pork trotter representative?”

“Pah, you’re talking about it in the worst way possible,” Zuo Cidian snorted and said. “Wang Chuanli will be discharged in a few days, and all four of his brothers are staying in the hospital to watch over him. There are also many patient’s family members outside the ICU. They certainly won’t be able to get their hands on any delicious food. So, if we send them some good food right now, they will be grateful to us. They will then owe us a favor.”
Lu Wenbin immediately understood. He glanced at the pot and said, “I’ll ask my men to send more pork trotters over, then. Should I give some to the family members of other patients too?”
“Might as well. Only giving them to the Wang brothers wouldn’t look good on us.”

“I’ll need to check my stock, then. I’m afraid that there won’t be enough pork trotters from carefully selected giant pigs.” Lu Wenbin whipped out his cell phone as he spoke. “The Wang brothers seem to enjoy a pretty good relationship. They’re keeping a watch on their brother in the hospital all the time.”

“Their relationship is pretty good,” Zuo Cidian gave a brief reply, and there was no way that he would talk about the entanglements and arguments between the Wang family members regarding their interests. Rich and powerful families were complicated, to begin with, and as a mere doctor, he had no intention of partaking in their drama. He did not even bother gossiping about it.

Meanwhile, Lu Wenbin was only concerned about his stock. He made a few consecutive phone calls before plopping onto a chair in a relaxed manner. There was a satisfied smile on his face. “What a good day. I operated on a patient with four severed fingers and managed to sell so many pork trotters.”
Zuo Cidian had a thought in his mind. “Did you make a lot of money?”

Lu Wenbin was brewing another pot of soup, and he pursed his lips as he smiled. “I’ll give you ten pork trotter coupons later. But you know, Doctor Zuo, you know a lot of people. If you could help me promote my business...”
“Forget about it. I’m still hoping to become an attending physician.” Zuo Cidian the old resident doctor waved in dismissal and said no to this suggestion that did not sound very attractive anyway.
Ling Ran drove back home in a leisurely manner.

After operating on the patient with four severed patients, it was no longer the peak traffic period after work. There were not many cars on the road, and Ling Ran did not have to be stuck in a jam as he drove his Volkswagen Jetta.
He opened the car window and breathed in some fresh air. He was in a pretty good mood.
Even though the system did not reward him fairly for his recent mission, he still felt very happy to have resuscitated so many patients back to back.

Ling Ran even started to recall the time when he was still a child. He would often watch patients get treated in the clinic. There were not many hospitals at that time, and patients had to go through complex procedures to receive treatment at a hospital. Hence, the responsibility to administer initial treatment and provide a diagnosis for patients fell on clinics, including Lower Groove Clinics. They had to take in many children with fever and adults with diarrhea at night. It was totally different from what was happening right now when people only went to clinics for fluid transfusions.
“I wonder how Doctor Miao is doing with his cosmetic surgery patients,” Ling Ran muttered as he slowly reversed his car into the parking lot.
It was nighttime, and there were only a few scattered patients in the clinic. Judging by the amount of liquid left in their fluid transfusion bottles, they would be leaving soon.

Ling Jiezhou had carried a reclining chair into the treatment room, and he looked like an old patient as he lay alongside the patients. He was chit-chatting with a few elderly men who were receiving a fluid transfusion.

Tao Ping was holding a bowl of peach resin desert. She sipped spoonfuls of it and listened as the men talked. She would chip in every now and then, and there was a smile on her face from the beginning to the end...
“I’m back,” Ling Ran called out. He sounded like he just got back from school.
“Eh? You’re back, son?” Tao Ping was surprised. “Didn’t you send me a text message saying that you’re working in the ICU?”
“Yup, but I’m done.” Ling Ran nodded.
“So... are you having dinner?” Tao Ping finished the peach resin dessert in her bowl and rose.
Ling Ran shook his head and said, “I had some pork trotters.”
“You can eat again later. Hm, why don’t you have a bowl of peach resin dessert first?” Tao Ping said and went to the kitchen.
Soon, Ling Jiezhou sent the last few patients away, and a delivery man from Haidilao came.
“We ordered this for you.” Ling Jiezhou asked the delivery man to set up the table and said with a smile on his face, “Your mom immediately called them after you got home.”

As he spoke, the delivery man placed the pot on the table and poured the broth into it. There were two broths, one was clear and the other was red. The delivery man then placed beef, mutton, fish paste, meatballs, pork intestines, and ox aorta on the table.
Soon, the table was full.
The delivery man said respectfully, “Mister Ling, because you ordered the meal six hours in advance, there’s a complimentary fruit platter. I’ll put it here—”
“It smells pretty good,” Ling Jiezhou quickly cut the delivery man off.

Hence, the delivery man lowered his head and continued setting up the table. Before he left, he said, “Mister Ling, I have also placed the additional set of cutleries on the table, so there are three sets in total. Do you need anything else?”

chapters.title: Chapter 913: Could Not Remain as Calm
paragraphs: The ICU, for most people, this place brought about endless despair.

They would enter the ICU in despair, receive treatment in despair, and hope to get better in despair. They would also be in despair when they see other patients leaving the ICU, as they wished to be in their place.
Young Feng, though, was used to being outside the ICU.

She was holding a large pork trotter and enjoying it. It was as if she was eating a rare culinary delight that was hard to come by. Truth be told, this was her best meal this week. The pork trotter was tender and flavorful, and the tendons could be bitten off in one bite. It was salty and aromatic due to the braised soup.
“If I knew that the hospital is selling pork trotters, I would have bought it every single day.” Young Feng was regretting her bad judgment.

Financially, she was not really in a bad place, or you could say that ever since she was young, she never felt the lack of money. Hence, even though her husband needed a lot of money for his treatment, Young Feng had the feeling that the money would eventually come back. This was because she grew up in a rich family.

So, even though they were not working and merely using up their savings, and even though their savings, which used to be seven figures, had gone down tremendously, Young Feng was not fretting too much over it.

However, Young Feng was feeling a little tired after taking care of her husband alone in the ICU for so many days. Sometimes, when she had the time, she would sit alone and read a book, sneak out and watch a movie or cry for no reason. After doing these things, she would feel better upon returning to the ICU.
“Madam Liu.” Doctor Yan had just exited the office, and he saw Young Feng sitting and eating a pork trotter alone. For some reason, he felt like greeting her.
“Doctor Yan.” Young Feng quickly wiped her mouth.

“Go ahead and continue eating. I’m just greeting you since you’re here.” Doctor Yan paused for a moment, and when he saw that Young Feng had placed the pork trotter back inside the plastic bag, he sat down and said with a smile, “You’ve not gone home for a few days. Why don’t you go back and take a good rest?”
“The hospital is my home now.” Young Feng flashed him a slight smile. It was an elegant one.

Doctor Yan could not help but be reminded of graceful female celebrities. When he first hit puberty, many of the graceful female leads in television series were virtuous and dutiful women. Doctor Yan could not get this image out of his mind, and Young Feng looked and acted just like one of them.
“Things are hard on you.” Doctor Yan sighed.

“People get sick. They also get old and die. There’s no helping it. Fortunately, people can only die once in their lives,” Young Feng spoke slowly, and her words left a lingering mark in Doctor Yan’s mind.
Doctor Yan shook his head. “Don’t think too much. Go back and rest. When the surgery comes, you won’t get to rest even if you want to.”

Young Feng was Young Dai’s only family member, and she would definitely have to wait outside the operating theater during the day of the surgery. And combined stomach and liver radical surgery would definitely take a long time.
Young Feng was a little tempted. She turned to look at the ICU and thought about it for a few seconds. She then nodded. “Alright, then. I’ll go back and wash up before coming back.”
Unlike ordinary family members of patients, she did not give the doctors a lot of reminders. She was also neither long-winded nor unable to make up her mind.

In Doctor Yan’s perfect world, every single family member would be like that. But Doctor Yan knew that Young Feng was only like this because she had gone through a lot in life. The more hope a person had, the more disappointed he would be.
“Doctor Ling will be personally operating on the patient, so the surgery will definitely go very well.” Doctor Yan had never said such things, but this time, he could not hold himself back.
As a doctor working in the ICU, Doctor Yan frequently tried to lower patients’ expectations. He would sometimes even extinguish the flicker of hope in patients’ hearts.
“It’s impossible for the patient to go back to the way he was before.”
“Total recovery is impossible.”
“If the patient is able to talk and understand what you guys are saying, it would be the best outcome already...”
Many times, while conversing with patients’ family members, Doctor Yan would use his words to show them how harsh reality was.
This time, however, Doctor Yan hoped that Young Feng could be more hopeful and fantasize more about things.
At least, fantasy would be more beautiful compared to reality.
Young Feng thanked Doctor Yan again. She smiled gracefully, and her smile lingered in Doctor Yan’s mind. “I hope so.”

“Doctor Ling is one of the top hepatectomy experts in Changxi province. There are even hospitals in Beijing hiring him for freelance surgery.” Doctor Yan did not want to say it, but he wanted to make Young Feng more confident in the surgery, and he was unable to hold himself back.

Young Feng’s experience changed a little. She looked at Doctor Yan. “I know that Doctor Ling is pretty excellent and that he frequently carries out freelance surgery in Wuxin City. But I didn’t know that he also operates on patients in Beijing...”

“He has done so more than once. From what I know, a department director of a General Surgery Department of a hospital in Beijing has specifically sought treatment from Doctor Ling. He was able to walk only a few days after the surgery, and he went overseas for treatment after that.” Doctor Yan lowered his voice a little and said in a mysterious tone, “You know, with the department director’s income and status, he would have had no problem seeking treatment overseas. But he ended up asking Doctor Ling to operate on him. So, it’s definitely a great thing that Doctor Ling is willing to operate on Yong Dai...”

Young Feng’s face slowly lit up as she listened to Doctor Yan’s words. She then realized that Doctor Yan was inching closer to her. She was embarrassed and said in a soft voice, “Doctor Yan, I have promised Young Dai that I would become a Buddhist nun if he dies before me...”
Doctor Yan was shocked. “Are there still... people who do this nowadays?”

Young Feng hummed softly in acknowledgment and said, “I’m not a good businesswoman. So, if Young Dai is no longer in this world, I’ll have to find a job. Nowadays, you have to get certified to become a Buddhist nun, so I’ll have a stable income. Moreover, if I stay in a temple, the other nuns and I can take care of each other, and I won’t have to resort to spending Chinese New Year alone...”
Doctor Yan did not know how to react.
On Tuesday at six in the morning, Operating Theater 1 was brightly lit.
Two circulating nurses walked back and forth from the operating theater to the supply room.
Combined stomach and liver radical surgery was a rare surgical method in Yun Hua Hospital, and this was the first time it was performed in the Emergency Medical Center.

It was not because it was a top-notch surgery. Of course, it was quite top-notch, as it was made up of two Level 4 surgeries and required the knowledge it took to perform many kinds of surgeries. People in the Emergency Medical Center were worried because of how long the surgery would take and the wide assortment of medical fields required for the surgery to work.

Even though senior medical scholars had created classifications for surgeries, medical staff members, especially those working in tertiary Grade A hospitals, had their own ways of classifying surgery.

According to the classification method commonly used in China, hemihepatectomy was already a major, Level 4 surgery. Total gastrectomy and gastrectomy for gastric cancer were also Level 4 surgeries. However, in tertiary Grade A hospitals nowadays, even though it was not easy to perform well in these kinds of surgeries, it was not hard for a doctor to launch this surgical method.

Even if a person were to disregard other things, the First People’s Hospital of Wuxin City and Second People’s Hospital of Wuxin City were launching many Level 4 surgeries by inviting Ling Ran over for freelance surgery all the time.
However, pure hepatectomy was obviously nothing compared to combined stomach and liver radical surgery.
At least, it was much more large-scale. In the field of medicine, the difficulty level of surgery increased exponentially the greater its scale and the longer its duration.
The scale, as well as the difficulty of the surgery, could be seen from the number of nurses and anesthetists in the operating theater.

“Ling Ran has never carried out hepatectomy plus gastrectomy for the treatment of gastric cancer, has he?” The department director of the General Surgery Department squinted as he sat in a chair in the visitation room. He even looked a little bit sleepy.

“I remember that years ago when you operated on a patient with intestinal obstruction for the first time, you didn’t receive guidance from anyone either. You followed the instructions on a book, right?” Huo Congjun smiled, and as usual, his words were offensive.

“Things were different back then.” The department director of the General Surgery Department smiled. This was one of the achievements that he was the most pleased with from his younger years. If he were a renowned person, this would be part of his biography.
Huo Congjun smiled too. “How different can it be?”

It was not a secret that in the hospital, resident doctors would refer to books as the prescribed medication, and attending physicians would flip through the pages as they operated on patients. It did not seem to be wrong for a person to refer to books when he did not know how to do something. This was especially true for rare illnesses and symptoms. Even chief physicians would have to refer to books when the situation called for it.
The department director of the General Surgery Department, though, pursed his mouth and said, “There didn’t use to be so many cell phones. There weren’t cameras in the operating theaters either.”

Huo Congjun’s expression changed a little, but he showed no signs of trepidation. “Ling Ran is one of the top surgeons for hepatectomy and gastrectomy. It’s only natural that he would give the challenge of combined stomach and liver radical surgery a try.”

“You know what? You’re right.” The department director of the General Surgery Department was not doubtful of Ling Ran’s abilities. Yet, he could not remain as calm as he looked on the surface when the Emergency Medical Center was carrying out an extremely high-end general surgery.
