She turned to look at the ICU and thought about it for a few seconds.
She then nodded.
“Alright, then.
I’ll go back and wash up before coming back.”
Unlike ordinary family members of patients, she did not give the doctors a lot of reminders.
She was also neither long-winded nor unable to make up her mind.
In Doctor Yan’s perfect world, every single family member would be like that.
But Doctor Yan knew that Young Feng was only like this because she had gone through a lot in life.
The more hope a person had, the more disappointed he would be.
“Doctor Ling will be personally operating on the patient, so the surgery will definitely go very well.” Doctor Yan had never said such things, but this time, he could not hold himself back.
As a doctor working in the ICU, Doctor Yan frequently tried to lower patients’ expectations.
He would sometimes even extinguish the flicker of hope in patients’ hearts.
“It’s impossible for the patient to go back to the way he was before.”
“Total recovery is impossible.”
“If the patient is able to talk and understand what you guys are saying, it would be the best outcome already...”
Many times, while conversing with patients’ family members, Doctor Yan would use his words to show them how harsh reality was.
This time, however, Doctor Yan hoped that Young Feng could be more hopeful and fantasize more about things.
At least, fantasy would be more beautiful compared to reality.
Young Feng thanked Doctor Yan again.
She smiled gracefully, and her smile lingered in Doctor Yan’s mind.
“I hope so.”
“Doctor Ling is one of the top hepatectomy experts in Changxi province.

There are even hospitals in Beijing hiring him for freelance surgery.” Doctor Yan did not want to say it, but he wanted to make Young Feng more confident in the surgery, and he was unable to hold himself back.
Young Feng’s experience changed a little.
She looked at Doctor Yan.
“I know that Doctor Ling is pretty excellent and that he frequently carries out freelance surgery in Wuxin City.
But I didn’t know that he also operates on patients in Beijing...”
“He has done so more than once.
From what I know, a department director of a General Surgery Department of a hospital in Beijing has specifically sought treatment from Doctor Ling.

He was able to walk only a few days after the surgery, and he went overseas for treatment after that.” Doctor Yan lowered his voice a little and said in a mysterious tone, “You know, with the department director’s income and status, he would have had no problem seeking treatment overseas.
But he ended up asking Doctor Ling to operate on him.
So, it’s definitely a great thing that Doctor Ling is willing to operate on Yong Dai...”
Young Feng’s face slowly lit up as she listened to Doctor Yan’s words.
She then realized that Doctor Yan was inching closer to her.
She was embarrassed and said in a soft voice, “Doctor Yan, I have promised Young Dai that I would become a Buddhist nun if he dies before me...”
Doctor Yan was shocked.
“Are there still... people who do this nowadays?”
Young Feng hummed softly in acknowledgment and said, “I’m not a good businesswoman.
So, if Young Dai is no longer in this world, I’ll have to find a job.
Nowadays, you have to get certified to become a Buddhist nun, so I’ll have a stable income.
Moreover, if I stay in a temple, the other nuns and I can take care of each other, and I won’t have to resort to spending Chinese New Year alone...”
Doctor Yan did not know how to react.
On Tuesday at six in the morning, Operating Theater 1 was brightly lit.
Two circulating nurses walked back and forth from the operating theater to the supply room.
Combined stomach and liver radical surgery was a rare surgical method in Yun Hua Hospital, and this was the first time it was performed in the Emergency Medical Center.
It was not because it was a top-notch surgery.
Of course, it was quite top-notch, as it was made up of two Level 4 surgeries and required the knowledge it took to perform many kinds of surgeries.
People in the Emergency Medical Center were worried because of how long the surgery would take and the wide assortment of medical fields required for the surgery to work.

Even though senior medical scholars had created classifications for surgeries, medical staff members, especially those working in tertiary Grade A hospitals, had their own ways of classifying surgery.
According to the classification method commonly used in China, hemihepatectomy was already a major, Level 4 surgery.
Total gastrectomy and gastrectomy for gastric cancer were also Level 4 surgeries.
However, in tertiary Grade A hospitals nowadays, even though it was not easy to perform well in these kinds of surgeries, it was not hard for a doctor to launch this surgical method.

Even if a person were to disregard other things, the First People’s Hospital of Wuxin City and Second People’s Hospital of Wuxin City were launching many Level 4 surgeries by inviting Ling Ran over for freelance surgery all the time.
However, pure hepatectomy was obviously nothing compared to combined stomach and liver radical surgery.
At least, it was much more large-scale.
In the field of medicine, the difficulty level of surgery increased exponentially the greater its scale and the longer its duration.
The scale, as well as the difficulty of the surgery, could be seen from the number of nurses and anesthetists in the operating theater.

“Ling Ran has never carried out hepatectomy plus gastrectomy for the treatment of gastric cancer, has he?” The department director of the General Surgery Department squinted as he sat in a chair in the visitation room.
He even looked a little bit sleepy.
“I remember that years ago when you operated on a patient with intestinal obstruction for the first time, you didn’t receive guidance from anyone either.
You followed the instructions on a book, right?” Huo Congjun smiled, and as usual, his words were offensive.
“Things were different back then.” The department director of the General Surgery Department smiled.
This was one of the achievements that he was the most pleased with from his younger years.
If he were a renowned person, this would be part of his biography.
Huo Congjun smiled too.
“How different can it be?”
It was not a secret that in the hospital, resident doctors would refer to books as the prescribed medication, and attending physicians would flip through the pages as they operated on patients.
It did not seem to be wrong for a person to refer to books when he did not know how to do something.
This was especially true for rare illnesses and symptoms.
Even chief physicians would have to refer to books when the situation called for it.
The department director of the General Surgery Department, though, pursed his mouth and said, “There didn’t use to be so many cell phones.
There weren’t cameras in the operating theaters either.”
Huo Congjun’s expression changed a little, but he showed no signs of trepidation.
“Ling Ran is one of the top surgeons for hepatectomy and gastrectomy.
It’s only natural that he would give the challenge of combined stomach and liver radical surgery a try.”
“You know what?
You’re right.” The department director of the General Surgery Department was not doubtful of Ling Ran’s abilities.
Yet, he could not remain as calm as he looked on the surface when the Emergency Medical Center was carrying out an extremely high-end general surgery.

chapters.title: Chapter 914: Plan
paragraphs: Yu Yuan walked forward in small steps, pushed open the door, and entered the visitation room. Then, she waved her hands behind her, and a bunch of young doctors followed her inside. The majority of them were medical interns and housemen.
Although the chairs at the center were empty, the interns and housemen still obediently stood by the sides and the back of the room.

While this was a major surgery that needed many doctors, Ling Ran’s group had a lot of young doctors. Therefore, no matter how people came over, they could not participate in the surgery, since they were not in Ling Ran’s group. They could only watch in the visitation room like doctors from other departments.

However, compared to other groups, these young doctors from Ling Ran’s treatment group had it easier. One, they could at least come and watch in the visitation room. Two, there was a difference in categorizing the young doctors in different departments and treatment groups.

The elite department like the General Surgery Department treated the attending physicians who were below thirty-five years old as junior doctors, and the attending physicians with low qualifications could do nothing about it as well.
Huo Congjun turned and glanced around. He pointed at the chair in front of him and said, “Take a seat, Doctor Yu. It’s still early now, not many people will come to watch the surgery.”

As he spoke, Huo Congjun introduced her to the department director of the General Surgery Department. “Doctor Yu is a postgraduate student who came to our department earlier on. She became a chief resident this year. You have performed quite a number of surgeries, right?”
Yu Yuan put on an obedient face and said, “I performed two surgeries in the morning.”

When the department director of the General Surgery Department heard this, he subconsciously took a look at the time and instantly came to a realization. “All of you work according to Doctor Ling’s schedule now, huh?”
“Yes, of course.” Yu Yuan tilted her head slightly and continued looking obedient.
The department director of the General Surgery Department gasped in amazement and looked at Huo Congjun. “Ling Ran is quite capable of training his doctors.”

This may have just been a small adjustment in working hours, but in a public general hospital, working hours usually corresponded to a leader’s authority. The foundation to be an expert department director was to make the subordinates work overtime when he wanted them to. However, many department directors from small hospitals could not fulfill even such a small requirement because the authority of the directors in the small department of small hospitals was really weak.

The powerful department directors could make their subordinates work overtime whenever necessary. Regardless of whether there was a reward or whether there was no reward in whether the subordinates obey them, when the order was given, they must follow it, and this was the standard of a director in a big department of big hospitals.

Furthermore, it was very difficult for them to make the whole department adjust their working hours according to the department director’s schedule, and it would be harder the more mature the department was.

Besides, the requests for their subordinates to change their working hours were basically an authority unique to department directors. Compared to the authority of department directors, the difficulty level in leaders of treatment groups asking their subordinates to change their working hours was even harder.

Even many treatment groups in big hospitals could not get enough manpower when the time came for them to do frequent overtime. When the group members tried every trick up their sleeves to take leave, many treatment group leaders who were not capable of managing their group would think that they never had a treatment group, to begin with. The would work, treating patients all over the place, so much so that their overtime hours surpassed their peers...
Huo Congjun never realized that Ling Ran’s management level was so unique. Right then, he wore a happy face and said, “Ling Ran is a manager with the charms of a leader.”

“That’s true.” The department director of the General Surgery Department praised him and nodded. He turned around and asked in a deliberately friendly tone, “Doctor Yu, what are the surgeries you performed in the morning?”
Yu Yuan continued being obedient. “One is an emergency appendectomy, and another one is—”
“Ahem.” Huo Congjun’s coughing was too loud, and all those who heard it knew it was fake.

The department director of the General Surgery Department frowned. Appendectomy was one of the projects of the General Surgery Department. Although they had long since not bothered themselves with small surgeries like appendectomy, listening to doctors from the Emergency Department talk about carrying out emergency appendectomy in front of him, who was the department director of the General Surgery Department, he would still feel displeased.

Emergency appendectomy? How much of an emergency could it be? The patient might be in pain, but based on the surgery choices he could make, he would have no problem in receiving his surgery even if he waited until the next day. While the department director was still young, he had seen many who would endure the pain for two to three days before coming for surgery treatment...
But while he was grumbling up a storm in his heart, the department director of the General Surgery Department was still more interested in the surgery that Yu Yuan did not say.
If she could even mention something like an emergency appendectomy, then what sort of surgery would make Huo Congjun actually take steps to stop it from being mentioned?
Intestinal obstruction repair? Hernia repair?
Did they perform a gastrointestinal repair instead?
The department director of the General Surgery Department became sterner and stared at Yu Yuan before he asked, ” What was the second surgery?”
Huo Congjun sighed and did not try to stop Yu Yuan anymore.
Yu Yuan replied frankly, “Rectal foreign body removal.”
The department director of the General Surgery Department was instantly stunned.

“It is a simpler one; a ping pong ball. Initially, the patient had a string connected to the ping pong ball, and he tried to pull it out with the thread, but he did not manage to get it out. The thread snapped instead. He came over for surgery at five o’clock in the morning, and we got it out after fifteen minutes.” Yu Yuan made a motion of pulling something out and said, “Actually it’s very hard to take out a normal ping pong ball, but luckily, this guy was smart and knew how to connect the ping pong ball with a thread. Besides, the ping pong ball was light, so it’s easier for me to get it out after I found the end of the thread.”
The department director of the General Surgery Department turned his head around laboriously and looked at Huo Congjun, who kept staring at him.
Huo Congjun’s expression turned from curiosity to excitement to seriousness to amusement he could not conceal to slight disgust. The range of emotions he expressed varied greatly.

The department director of the General Surgery Department’s expression was quite funny as well. His expression changed from awkwardness to helplessness, then from resignation to realization, and from realization to embarrassment and annoyance.
“Observe the surgery.”
“Observe the surgery.”
The two department directors first put aside their funny and amusing expressions, and they received support from the people around them, who all looked disgusted.
“Do we need to perform surgery like this in the future?” a new intern from Ling Ran’s group whispered into the ears of an “old” intern, Qi Zao.
Qi Zao replied to him with a smile, “Don’t worry, we won’t.”
“Really?” The new intern sensed an unexpected delight.
Qi Zao nodded seriously. “Of course. It’s already difficult for you to get the position of an assistant, so there’s no way you can have the chance to get such a rare surgery.”
The new intern wanted to flip tables.
At the operating theater were Ling Ran, Zhang Anmin, Lu Wenbin, and Ma Yanlin. They were in their respective places, and their expressions were serious.

This was the strongest lineup in Ling Ran’s treatment group. In fact, this could be considered as the strongest hepatectomy lineup in Yun Hua Hospital. If this happened two years ago, Lu Wenbin and the others could still be considered as newbies, but as they continued performing hepatectomy with Ling Ran for two years, the number of hepatectomies participated by Lu Wenbin and the others was among the top in the hospital.
If they put in a broader perspective, perhaps they could even say that the number of hepatectomies was at the top of the province.

Certainly, the medical world did not care about the total surgery volume of the assistants. But in terms of practical ability, Lu Wenbin and the others were already more than skilled enough to become the assistants in hepatectomy. Currently, Zhang Anmin, who had become an associate department director of the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery, already had skills and qualifications that were almost at the level of a chief surgeon.
However, this was a gastrectomy in combination with hepatic resection, and it was performed by a single surgeon, so they would never go overboard no matter how much preparation work they did.
Zhang Anmin looked at Ling Ran, and he smiled like a Golden Retriever.
“Gastrectomy in combination with hepatic resection, ready to start now.” Ling Ran’s expression was similarly serious.
Unlike the hepatectomy that Ling Ran was used to, the outcome of the surgical treatment for hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer was uncertain, and there was still not a standard guide until now.

This was because hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer was not similar to hepatic metastasis from colonic carcinoma. Hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer had a low resection rate and a high recurrence rate, and those two alone were bad indicators. Therefore, many doctors and patients now tended to go for comprehensive treatment, such as systemic chemotherapy, intervention chemotherapy, ablation treatment, molecularly targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. They might even go for multiple treatments.
Although no treatment plan was the most perfect and complete, among all treatment plans, surgery was definitely the one with the highest risk.
But if it were well performed, surgery would be the most beneficial treatment plan.

chapters.title: Chapter 915: The Bugle for Victory
paragraphs: “Pen.” Ling Ran extended his hand before pulling it back. He started to draw lines on the patient’s body.
An extremely long incision line was drawn, and it looked as if Ling Ran wanted to open up the patient’s entire abdominal cavity.
Since Ling Ran would be working on the liver and stomach, the patient’s abdominal cavity would have to be basically completely opened.
Those nurses and assistants who were there subconsciously became serious as they observed Ling Ran drawing the line.
Any hospital or operating theater would treat this matter with seriousness when they had to perform a surgery with such a huge incision.
Ling Ran’s expression was even more serious.

He had already opened Young Dai’s abdominal cavity multiple times through the Virtual Human. He already knew the insides of the patient’s abdomen with his eyes closed. Even so, when he was about to really start such a complicated surgery, he still did not dare say that he was completely confident.

Constant repetitions needed to be done so that he could remember every detail, and he had to be accurate right down to the second. Then, during the moment of true battle, he could get the best results. This was a gamer’s mentality.
The reality was always much more complicated.
Forget about the patient’s stress reaction, the ability of how well his anesthetist and assistants could cooperate with him was already something of a constant mystery.
After being a doctor for a long time, one would know that sometimes, not only would people get odd illnesses, they would even make odd mistakes.

Even if everything went smoothly, the progress of the surgery and its direction would still be uncertain. Accidents happened frequently when there were a lot of steps in the surgery, and the surgery time was long.

They always said that a person would make three hundred minor mistakes before a major one. Even if a person did not die on the operating table, that did not mean that everything on the operating table went in an orderly and smooth manner.

Regardless of how high the level of a surgeon was, they would neither be able to prevent strange changes in the patient’s body nor predict whether the blood products imported into the patient’s body would change, let alone whether the anesthetist could complete all his maneuvers during a surgery perfectly.
What made Ling Ran most uncertain was the patients’ prognosis.
He could use a Virtual Human to influence the surgery, but the prognosis of the surgery could not be predicted.

The reason why surgical treatment for hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer faced many problems was because of poor prognosis. Of course, any current treatment method for hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer would still produce a poor prognosis.
The low five-year survival rate that was between ten percent to fifteen percent was like a sword hanging over the head of patients with hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer.

Even if Ling Ran made sure that all lesion was removed cleanly, he could not be certain whether cancer would recur or metastasize. Of course, the strictest tumor-free operation could reduce the probability of metastasis, but the possibility would still exist.
Due to this, there were still debates for the surgical treatment of hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer.

Many doctors preferred palliative surgeries. They had to deal with bleeding, perforation, and obstruction caused by the tumor, improve the treatment for the patient’s survival, and prolong the patient’s survival time.
Ling Ran also had a plan for this.
After all, anything could happen when the patient’s abdominal cavity was opened.
“Scalpel.” There were a myriad of thoughts in Ling Ran’s mind as his hands still moved according to the established steps.
Zhang Anmin and the other assistants fixed their gazes on the surgical area like large dogs staring at a bowl of rice.

Su Jiafu also kept his eyes on the screen as he watched his associate chief physician increase and decrease the dosage. Today’s surgery was too big. Even if Ling Ran agreed to it, Su Jiafu himself did not dare to do it on his own.
The scalpel cut through the skin, and the skin curled up slightly like the crust of bread.
The yellowish fat layer had a trendy, grainy look and greasy look belonging to well-oiled antiques. When illuminated by the shadowless lamp, it gave off a timeless scent.
“I’m glad he’s not fat,” Zhang Anmin whispered, which made the atmosphere a little less tense.

Lu Wenbin looked up at Zhang Anmin and snuck a glance at Ma Yanlin, who was next to him. ‘Look at Zhang Anmin. He became really different after being an associate chief physician. He is braver at telling jokes in the visitation room no matter how many people are in there, even if the jokes are not interesting. Nowadays, people are so flighty. How can they consider the associate chief physician of the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery as a true associate chief physician? Department Director He Yuanzheng from the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery is now looking for a successor. The fool doesn’t even know how to learn some skills from Doctor Ling.

‘Besides, now that Zhang Anmin is an associate chief physician, he’s still flattering Doctor Ling. How shameless is this associate chief physician’s face? With this much salary, can’t he get some good quality face masks for himself? Even I, who cooks two pots of pork trotters, know how to do skincare...’
Ma Yanlin: Unamused face.jpg
“The situation sure is complicated.” Zhang Anmin waited for Ling Ran to open up the patient’s abdominal cavity before he sighed beside him. His main purpose was to assist Ling Ran.
Without opening the abdomen, there was no way for them to know just how complicated was the insides of a patient with hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer.
The reason why Zhang Anmin specifically said this was to support Ling Ran.
Just as he expected, Ling Ran hummed and only reminded him to pay attention to suction. He then immersed himself in the surgery.

He had practiced the first few steps through a Virtual Human. For today’s surgery, Lin Ran spent twenty minutes on the Virtual Human. After recklessly chiseling and cutting into the Virtual Human, he gained very clear knowledge about what he should for the first few steps.

However, the later stage of the surgery was always the most accident-prone. He also only had a limited time with the Virtual Human. It was impossible to rely on a Virtual Human for this kind of surgery, which often could take several hours. So, Ling Ran was extremely careful during the whole process.

Radical surgery could only be carried out if everything went well. Otherwise, the significance of the surgery would be very small, and it may not prolong the patient’s survival time as long as palliative surgery.
Ling Ran really wanted to achieve the goal of performing radical surgery.
This was the real advantage of surgical treatment.
No matter how high the two-year or five-year survival rates of other treatment plans were, in the end, all other treatment plans were palliative treatments and could only prolong the survival period.
Only surgical treatment plans granted the possibility of curing the patients.

The odds were low, even lower than winning a lottery. However, Ling Ran had gathered a whole arsenal of weapons and acquired Perfect Level Tissue Separation. Was this not so that he could increase the probability of winning the lottery?
“Gauze,” Ling Ran straightened his back and gave instructions in a soft voice with an indifferent expression.
Young Feng was in Yun Hua Emergency Medical Center’s waiting area. Her anxious expression was super obvious.

A middle-aged man noticed Young Feng, and he found himself fancying her. He could not help but went to her and handed her a piece of corn. He said with a smile, “I noticed that you have been here for some time. I bet you haven’t eaten your breakfast. I brought a lot of corn. Why don’t you fill your stomach with it for now?”
“Thank you, but I don’t need it.” Young Feng shook her head, showing the tender side of a Jiangnan woman.

An extremely long incision line was drawn, and it looked as if Ling Ran wanted to open up the patient’s entire abdominal cavity.
Since Ling Ran would be working on the liver and stomach, the patient’s abdominal cavity would have to be basically completely opened.
Those nurses and assistants who were there subconsciously became serious as they observed Ling Ran drawing the line.
Any hospital or operating theater would treat this matter with seriousness when they had to perform a surgery with such a huge incision.
Ling Ran’s expression was even more serious.

Even so, when he was about to really start such a complicated surgery, he still did not dare say that he was completely confident.
Constant repetitions needed to be done so that he could remember every detail, and he had to be accurate right down to the second.
Then, during the moment of true battle, he could get the best results.
This was a gamer’s mentality.
The reality was always much more complicated.
Forget about the patient’s stress reaction, the ability of how well his anesthetist and assistants could cooperate with him was already something of a constant mystery.

He is braver at telling jokes in the visitation room no matter how many people are in there, even if the jokes are not interesting.

Department Director He Yuanzheng from the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery is now looking for a successor.

chapters.title: Chapter 916: Tender
paragraphs: The patients’ family members in the waiting room came and went and came again.

Some patients’ surgeries finished faster, and their family members left in an hour or two. For patients’ whose surgeries lasted for three or four hours, their family members would have to wait in agony for longer.
Young Feng was the earliest one in the waiting room. She had waited here from morning until noon, but Young Dai was not wheeled out of the operating theater yet.
Even though the lengthy period of the surgery was talked about multiple times during the preoperative consultation, when this happened for real, Young Feng’s imagination could not help but run wild.

“Remember to pay attention to his health after going back. Do take note of the time when he passes urine...” Zhao Leyi walked into the corridor alongside a patient. He took off his mouth face mask and started telling the patient about things to pay attention to.
Young Feng was a little envious when she saw this.

In the past, when Young Dai first got sick, she was a little fearful of this scene. Every time she woke up in the middle of the night and thought about how Young Dai would eventually be wheeled out of the operating theater too, she felt a sharp pang in her heart.

At that time, Young Feng felt that even the healthiest people would become weak after going through a surgery, and they might not be able to recover completely even after a few years. There might also be sequelae.

Every time she thought about how Young Dai who was as strong as a bull would become tremendously frail with body aches and have difficulty sleeping after his surgery... Young Feng would feel uncomfortable.

However, now that she was looking at a patient who had just gone through surgery and his family members, Young Feng was thinking about how nice it would be if Young Dai could be wheeled out like this.
She did not mind at all that her husband would need a few years to recuperate. She wanted as many years together with him as possible.

“Is your husband not out yet?” A middle-aged man had seen his aunt being wheeled out quite some time ago. The lady had merely hit a van while she was riding her motorbike, and she ended up breaking her arm. Her injury did not seem very serious. However, the surgery took quite a long time because of the time taken to nail all the broken fragments of her bones together. Moreover, a lot of glass shards had gotten into her flesh.

Since his aunt had her children with her, he did not bother to go forward. Instead, he turned to look at Young Feng. He saw that she was sitting in a proper manner, and she looked as elegant and lovable as possible. He could not help but be tempted to chat her up.
He made his intention obvious, and Young Feng merely hummed flatly in acknowledgment.

The middle-aged man did not mind. He thought that Young Feng merely did not want to talk too much to a stranger. He whipped out his name card, handed it to Young Feng, and said with a smile, “I was worried that you would think that I’m old-fashioned just now, so I didn’t do this. Now that I have to leave, I’m giving you my name card. Give me a call if you need me. I’m not a rich man, and I’m the owner of a business that sells frozen products. Don’t think too much about it. Since we’ve met each other here, why don’t we be friends?”
Young Feng turned around wearily, and she did not even bother to say anything.
The middle-aged man stayed calm even though he was ignored. He consoled himself by comparing this incident to being ignored by a woman on Tantan.

He then placed his name card on the chair and smiled amiably. “My email address and my new QQ ID are on the name card. All of them are secure channels, and you can contact me if you need anything. Alright, I need to go now. See you again when you have time.”

Young Feng was a little furious and embarrassed at the same time, but there was no one she could throw a tantrum in front of. She recalled the times she spent together with her husband and could not help but tear up.
“Who’s family member is this?” Zhao Leyi who had just operated on the middle-aged man’s aunt saw Young Feng crying, and he felt a slight pang in his heart.
It was so heartbreaking to see such a beautiful woman cry like this.
The nurse beside him was a little uncomfortable with his attitude. She pouted and said, “The patient whom Doctor Ling picked up from the ICU.”

“The one who’s in Operating Theater 1 right now?” Zhao Leyi knew which patient it was immediately. When combined stomach and liver radical surgery was mentioned on the schedule on the wall in the Operating Area, the words were practically shining. These words were automatically bolded and italicized by all the doctors’ minds.

The young nurse hummed in acknowledgment and said, “I heard that she left her rich family and eloped with her husband. They did not get to live a good life together for long before her husband got sick.”

“No wonder. She seems rather pitiful.” Zhao Leyi merely looked at her and did not dare to talk to her. Who knew if his wife had taken his money and bought a few handbags to bribe the nurses in the hospital to watch over him?
The young nurse rolled her eyes and said, “Looking at women is all guys know how to do. Do you think that she’s feeling so sad just to seduce you guys?”
Zhao Leyi only regained his senses then, and he could not help but laugh. “You’re the one saying that she’s not feeling sad just to seduce guys, aren’t you? Then why aren’t you treating her nicely?”
“I’m not treating her badly. I just don’t like the sight of her!”
“Then, why are you speaking out on her behalf?”
“Because a**holes like you have no right to look down on women,” the young nurse said firmly.

This was not Zhao Leyi’s first time interacting with a young nurse, and he knew that he would never win in this kind of conversation. He said cleverly, “I just remembered that I have something to do in the operating theater.”
“He naturally had nothing to do in the operating theater, but compared to the corridor, the operating theater seemed like a better place for surgeons to stay in.
Zhao Leyi walked around the Operating Area in a leisurely manner. Even though he passed by the door of Operating Theater 1 twice, he suppressed his curiosity and did not go in.
So what if it was a major surgery?
It was only breaking news because hepatectomy and gastrectomy were carried out at the same time.
Of course, even if they were separated, hepatectomy and gastrectomy were both still major surgeries.

However, it was not like hepatectomy was anything to brag about. A surgeon merely had to expose the liver, interrupt the blood flow, cut off the diseased part of the liver, stitch the liver up, and close the abdominal cavity. If it were not for the fact that people were fragile and died easily, Zhao Leyi could perform hepatectomy too.

“Doctor Zhao, do you want a pork trotter?” The chef in the small canteen in the Operating Area was hired by the Emergency Medical Center. Ever since Ling Ran started carrying out hepatectomy, the income of the Emergency Department kept increasing. Now that it had been elevated to an Emergency Medical Cancer, their income was even higher. As a result, everyone in the department enjoyed excellent treatment.
COMMENT

In certain months, there would be too many patients funding their own treatment, and Huo Congjun would need to spend some energy discussing how to spend the money with Zuo Cidian. If they were unable to find good reasons to spend the money, they would need to hand it over to the hospital. When this happened, the money would be distributed evenly to the doctors in the entire hospital as a bonus.
Of course, they had no choice but to hand over part of the money. But they always tried to hand over as little money as possible
They hired this chef as part of their effort to spend their money.
He was merely a temporary worker who was not officially employed, and his pay was not high either. But he was a very diligent worker, and he even helped Lu Wenbin carry his pork trotters.
Zhao Leyi hesitated for a moment, but when he smelled the fragrant aroma of the pork trotters, he could not help but purchase one and pay via WeChat.
He lifted the pork trotter to his mouth and took a large bite, filling his mouth with a large chunk of pork. He chewed forcefully as if he was chewing Lu Wenbin’s ankle.
Zhao Leyi wrinkled his nose and asked, “Where’s Young Lu?”
“Doctor Lu? He’s carrying out surgery today. He was super excited about it.” The chef pointed at the large screen above their heads.
Zhao Leyi looked over and saw an exposed liver that looked extremely bloody. A few hands were tinkering with it.
Zhao Leyi’s expression instantly froze.
The new chef knew nothing about the power struggle in the department, and he said with pride, “I heard that it’s one of the most high-end surgeries in the country. A lot of people are watching it.”
“The surgery is still ongoing.” Zhao Leyi twisted his lips and sneered internally. ‘It’s easy to boast about something, but nobody knows how things are going to end yet.’

This was when Doctor Zhou, who was browsing TikTok in a corner, said, “It’s going quite smoothly. It seems like combined stomach and liver radical surgery isn’t really that difficult for Ling Ran. We’ll just see how the patient’s prognosis is like.”
Zhao Leyi turned abruptly. “When did you get here?”
Doctor Zhou scrolled his cell phone in a languid manner. He spoke slowly, like an old man, “When did I come to work again?”
Zhao Leyi who had just finished two surgeries did not know whether to be angry or grateful toward Doctor Zhou over the fact that he allowed his colleagues to seize the opportunities he passed over.
Before Zhao Leyi could say anything, naive resident doctors beside him started whispering among themselves. “Why do surgeries seem so easy when Doctor Ling is the one doing them?”
“It seems that more than one hundred users are watching this surgery on the live streaming platform of Yunli Medical Company.”
“Doctor Ling is the only one in our hospital who’s capable of performing this surgical method, isn’t he? Wait, no. Is there anyone else who can do the same in our province?”
Zhao Leyi gave them a sidelong glance and took another bite of the pork trotter. Pork trotters were usually tender, but today, it felt as hard as a rock to Zhao Leyi.
“I’m going to go outside.” Zhao Leyi put down his pork trotter and wiped his mouth. He was about to head to Operating Theater 1.

“You’ve just eaten a pork trotter. Remember to wash your hands, the pork trotter is oily.” Doctor Zhou straightened up and sighed. He then massaged his aching neck and stood up. “Hey, what’s your name again? Pack up a few pork trotters for me. Choose larger ones, and put one pork trotter in each plastic bag.”
“Are you planning to bring them home?” the chef asked.
“For doctors, the hospital is their home.” Doctor Zhou snorted and said, “I’m going to bring some food over to my father’s.”

chapters.title: Chapter 917: Faithful and True
paragraphs: In the afternoon, the visitation room of the Yun Hua Emergency Medical Center was overcrowded.

The doctors in the hospital during the afternoon were relatively free. If the young doctors still had various cases, reports, examination authorization forms, and other forms to fill in, the middle-ranked and senior doctors would be able to catch their breath at this time. They could then do something they like such as have casual meals, listen to music, swipe TikTok, tease young nurses, perform surgeries, or perform surgeries while teasing young nurses, listening to music, swiping TikTok, and having extra meals...
Many doctors also had to wait until this period before they could take time to look at Ling Ran’s combined stomach and liver radical surgery.
At this time, it was also the time when the operation was at its climax. Most doctors’ attention was also placed in the operating theater, not the visitation room.
“It looks like he’s not preparing to perform a palliative surgery.”

“He has already reached this step, why do you think he would be preparing the patient for palliative care? Furthermore, young doctors like Ling Ran are more radical, they’re more radical one after another.”
“He has to be skilled and lucky if he wants to be radical. Let’s see whether he can completely remove the metastases.”
During the discussion, the door of the visitation room was gently pushed open again.
Doctor Zhou looked inside before he walked to the first row with his back bent.
“Department Director Huo.” Doctor Zhou bent his knees while he stood in front of him. He handed out a lunch box with light movements and smiled. “Please fill your stomach.”
After observing the operation for a day, Huo Congjun smelled the familiar aroma of pork trotters and immediately felt hungry. He could not even refuse even if he subconsciously wanted to.

“Why did you buy something that smells so fragrant?” That being said, Huo Congjun still opened the lid reflexively. He could care less about the smell that was permeating the air which provoked the stomachs of the guests who came to grumble.
Doctor Zhou smiled in an aggrieved and bashful manner. “I was thinking that you like to eat this pork trotter, but I didn’t think about the strong smell...”

“Well. It’s okay. How many pork trotters did you buy?” Huo Congjun had actually just casually thrown a remark to criticize Doctor Zhou a little, but in truth, he did not care what other people could smell. The entire visitation room was funded by him. The effort he had thrown into building it, in the beginning, was equal to the amount of freedom he enjoyed now.
“Six.”
“Good, not bad,” Huo Congjun solemnly praised Doctor Zhou.

Doctor Zhou was experienced in trying to understand the thoughts of his “fathers”. During certain moments, one of his “fathers”, Huo Congjun would definitely be unwilling to follow the books and be a good gentleman.
For example, he never liked to pay attention to every detail when it came to the details of giving gifts.
“Here, have a pork trotter.” Huo Congjun handed a food box containing a pork trotter directly into the arms of the department director of the General Surgery Department.
“How can you be eating pork trotters at such times?” The department director of the General Surgery Department’s expression was full of resignation.

“If you don’t eat the pork trotter, won’t you get hungry?” Huo Congjun snorted and said, “This is a pork trotter made by a young doctor in our department, and he had been making the stew for two or three years...”
The department director of the General Surgery Department nodded. “I know, it’s Lu Wenbin’s pork trotters.”
“Oh my, the reputation of our Emergency Department’s pork trotters spread so fast?” Huo Congjun snickered.
The department director of the General Surgery Department smiled. “The house he bought is in the same area as my son’s.”
“Oh...” Huo Congjun drawled, but he did not seem interested. He was not so concerned about things outside the hospital.
There were a total of six pork trotters. Two were taken by Huo Congjun, and the remaining four were sent to the four doctors present.
He did not distribute them according to the status of the doctors, but according to how much he liked them.

Therefore, the doctor who received the pork trotters knew that he was liked by Huo Congjun. As for the chief physician or associate chief physicians who did not get the pork trotters, they had nothing to complain about either. They could only smell the aroma of the pork trotters, which made their stomachs rather worked up.

“It tastes good.” The department director of the General Surgery Department did not want to share his pork trotter. Even if he could share his pork trotter, he could not share his mistresses with others, no? If he could not share his mistresses with others, why should he share his pork trotter? In this case, the department director should just be an ally of the Emergency Department with peace in his mind. Sharing? It was impossible for him to share his pork trotter with people who were not allies with the Emergency Department.
Inside the visitation room, the smell of Lu Wenbin’s pork trotters permeated the air.
The department director of the General Surgery Department, Huo Congjun and others were eating pork trotters while laughing.
Other doctors drooled, and their gazes were just and impartial as they looked at the pork trotters, just like government officials.
Doctor Zhou ate till he was full before he casually sat down on a half the seat of a chair, but now, he felt more motivated to watch the surgery below.

“Ling Ran... seriously...” Regardless of whether Doctor Zhou could perform this type of surgery, his judgment was not bad. After just looking at it for a while, he could not help but glance at the department director of the General Department from the corner of his eyes.

In Yun Hua Hospital, the best and most high-end surgeon in the General Surgery Department was naturally this man, and Doctor Zhou’s most familiar benchmark was the department director of the General Surgery Department.

In Doctor Zhou’s memories, it had been a few years ago since the department director of the General Surgery Department performed surgery as cleanly and smoothly as Ling Ran. Furthermore, it was not necessarily such a high-level operation as the current one.
“Ling Ran has improved again.” Doctor Zhou was not foolish. Since he had the opportunity to show his face in front of Department Director Huo, he would not lose the opportunity.

Huo Congjun smiled, acknowledged it, and said, “It’s like this, look at his maneuvers, and you’ll know that it’s obvious that he has become more familiar with them. There are not many cases of combined liver and pancreatic radical surgery performed in the province in a year. In the end, it depends on how efficient a person can learn and how much he can obtain from each practice, the one who learns in the most efficient way and benefits the most reaches the highest level.”
Doctor Zhou pretended as if he was listening, but all of his muscles had relaxed, and his brain entered energy-saving mode.
In Operating Theater 1, Zhang Anmin also wished that he could enter energy-saving mode.
This was the longest operation he had ever performed. None of them had been this long before.
Just reading from books and watching videos could not clearly convey the demanding requirements of the surgeon’s physical strength and spirit required in a surgery lasting for seven to eight hours.
Zhang Anmin felt that his physical strength was already reaching its limit.

Usually, he also had to perform surgeries for four to five hours, sometimes even seven to eight hours straight. However, emergency operations where the work was handed over to others like a relay race and a surgery that went on like a long-distance race was, at the end of the day, vastly different.
Zhang Anmin gritted his teeth and looked at the chief surgeon, Ling Ran.
Ling Ran was stripping the blood vessels. His eyes were focused and serious, and there was no sign of tiredness.
It was obviously impossible for such a young person to suffer from backache like his. His back was already hurting so much that he could no longer persevere.
Zhang Anmin thought as he shook his head helplessly. Performing such an operation at such an age was a rare scene in itself.
In contrast, an associate chief physician of his age was more common.
“Wipe my sweat,” Zhang Anmin said in a low voice.
The nurse immediately stepped forward and used gauze to wipe his sweat.
Zhang Anmin took the opportunity to say, “Doctor Ling, would you like to take a short break?”
The operation time was indeed too long. When a doctor needed to rest, he had to be allowed to rest.
However, Ling Ran shook his head decisively. “I don’t need to rest, you can switch when you’re tired.”
He was in his most comfortable state at this time. Although the difficulty of the operation was getting higher and higher, yet Ling Ran’s interest for it gradually grew.
An ordinary hepatectomy was not as complicated as what he was doing now.
In order to remove the metastases cleanly and leave room for the remnant liver to grow, Ling Ran must design the path very carefully and determine the resection area ...
Considering the patient’s tolerance, Ling Ran’s movement during the operation was defter than usual.
The camera faithfully transmitted the surgical image.
The number of live broadcasts from Yunli Medical Company also jumped up one by one.

chapters.title: Chapter 918: Long Thinking Session
paragraphs: “Currently, the most viewed live stream in the live stream platform of Yunli Medical Company is Yun Hua Hospital’s surgery.” A resident doctor who looked so plain that his name was hard to remember guessed Huo Congjun’s thoughts and buttered up to him to increase his sense of existence.

When Huo Congjun wanted to turn and look at the one who spoke, he heard the department director of the General Surgery Department chuckle and say, “Those who hear about surgeries like combined liver and pancreatic radical surgery would want to see it. How should I comment on this mentality, I wonder...?”

When he heard what the department director of the General Surgery Department said, Huo Congjun naturally turned around and looked at him. As the department director of the Emergency Medical Center, although Huo Congjun scolded someone every day, he still had to behave politely when he should.

The resident doctor who only came up with a suitable topic after thinking for two hours looked at Huo Congjun’s back in disappointment, and he could not help but think about his friend’s teasing words, ‘He’ll remember you if you slap him.’
“They’re searching for novelty, huh?”

Since the department director spoke, the doctors from the General Surgery Department in the room naturally needed to show support. One of them even had to guess the director’s mood and took a tentative step forward in the conversation.

Combined liver and pancreatic radical surgery was a surgery that fit into every single criterion in the field of general surgery. Even if the Department of Hepatobiliary and Pancreatic Surgery wanted to work on it, they also needed to give away the stomach to the General Surgery Department, then both sides would work together to perform the surgery...
What else were they supposed to do? Were they supposed to let one single person get such good surgery and chances to become famous alone? That would be a waste.

Huo Congjun glanced around and saw the doctor from the General Surgery Department who spoke. He was a sleazy man who looked quite old, and his mouth drooped like a Shar-pei, and it made people want to laugh at him.
Huo Congjun did not have any memory of him, and this could mean that he was probably an attending physician with low qualifications, so he did not deserve Old Huo’s personal scolding.
Therefore, Department Director Huo Congjun wore a faint smile that meant, “I will temporarily spare your head.”

Doctor Zhou glanced at Huo Congjun, and for some inexplicable reason, he thought of the adjectives that he read in a novel a few days ago. He thought, ‘Could this be what you call a ghost of a smile while your eyes sparkle?

Doctor Zhou could not help falling into deep thought. The dazed expression he showed just now was gone, and he seemed to have been refilled with energy. He reentered the state where his heart rate slowed down and his breathing became light.

Yu Yuan said from the side, “The combined liver and pancreatic radical surgery by Doctor Ling is different from any other. Surgery is not suitable for the patient with hepatic metastasis from gastric cancer mainly because his body is too weak, and his tolerance for surgery is low. In this regard, Doctor Ling’s Ling Hepatectomy is very suitable...”
“You’re the only one who calls it Ling Hepatectomy, right?” the old-looking resident doctor with low qualifications could not help but quip sarcastically.
Yu Yuan chuckled. “This is the treatment plan recognized in the province, and it is quite famous in the country. If you can’t accept it, you’re welcome to write an article to refute my words.”
“We’re working in the same hospital, so how can I write an article to refute you...?”

“Can’t you, though?” Yu Yuan jumped down from her chair. She slowly stood up straight. Although there was no change in her height, and she even looked shorter because she was now standing, she actually appeared imposing now.
Yu Yuan never felt scared when she did not have to talk about surgeries and only had to talk about research articles alone.
When the junior attending physician across her faced her and looked at her, he really felt diffident.

In the chain of contempt in the hospital, it was politically correct for the General Surgery Department to regard the Emergency Medical Center in contempt, but there were also differences in the levels of the doctors from different departments. If those who were skilled and capable of engaging in technical work and people who were considered third-class people because they could only butter up to others were about the same level and there was not a huge difference between their ranks, they would still have a balance in their hearts weighing their worth.
“It’s just a casual remark. I can’t write an article just to scold someone, right?” The young attending physician puffed and retorted. He was not willing to admit defeat.
Yu Yuan said, “What’s wrong with scolding people using an article? Even Lu Xun wrote articles to scold people.”
Huo Congjun said, “Be responsible for what you say.”
The two of them spoke almost simultaneously, and they stared at the young attending physician with a sharp gaze.
The young attending physician’s face flushed red.
The department director of the General Surgery Department cast Huo Congjun a sidelong glance, and his expression was clearly saying, ‘Are you serious about being responsible for what you said?’
“Take note in checking the blood vessel. 7-0 surgical suture.” At that moment, Ling Ran had started to do circular suture around the liver tissues.

There was no big difference between the steps in hepatectomy for hepatic metastasis and normal hepatectomy, but in this case, ensuring a tumor-free operation was no longer something the surgeon needed to remind himself to do, but something he really needed to pay attention to.
With the patient’s condition, he could not afford another relapse and another hepatectomy.
Ling Ran also stopped for a while once he reached this point, then he started to use his Virtual Human to make a direct observation by cutting it open and checking it.

This was absolutely considered to be cheating. If this were a competition between two doctors, the doctor who did this would be the same as him trampling on sportsmanship. However, for the patient, if the doctor had this trick and decided not to use it, the doctor would be considered to be trampling on the patient’s life.
Ling Ran looked slightly dazed.
After all, his attention was on the Virtual Human now.
The doctors in the visitation room turned from feeling calm to feeling puzzled, and they started discussing among themselves.
“Did something go wrong?”
“No matter how I look at it, it was progressing smoothly.”
“Where is the problem?”
Everyone’s proactiveness was awakened. They paid full attention to the surgery and observed it while they recalled the process of the surgery.
If they could catch Ling Ran’s mistake, their fame would definitely increase.
Yu Yuan pursed her lips in contempt. She stood straight and said, “Doctor Ling has a habit when he performs surgery. He often descends into a state where he thinks for a long time.

“It’s just like a Go player. When you play to the point where it’s time to decide the victor, you need to consider information from different perspectives before making a comprehensive judgment. While you’re thinking at this moment, you might already be considering his next thirty to forty steps.
“Doctor Ling is also like this.”
The doctors in the visitation room were immediately no longer puzzled.

When Yu Yuan saw this, she raised her head and described the situation to them. She said, “Doctor Ling’s thinking period varies. The shortest is about a dozen seconds, and if it’s long, it can last for a few minutes. When we were in Beijing performing surgery for a patient, Doctor Ling thought for two minutes. The doctor from Beijing who worked with us thought that Doctor Ling had been intimidated, so he walked away to wash his hands. But in the end, once Doctor Ling finished thinking, he finished the surgery in just a short while. The doctor who washed his hands came back in time to help clean up the operating theater. Hahaha!”
Yu Yuan’s laughter was obviously louder than her height, and her laughter was easily recognizable, causing a few doctors to laugh with her, because it would be embarrassing if they did not.
“So, standing aside to daydream and practice Tai Chi during the middle of surgery is also a habit of Doctor Ling’s?” a doctor standing at the back row took the opportunity to ask during the chaos.
Yu Yuan subconsciously looked at the lower floor. Indeed, Ling Ran had taken a few steps back while he moved hands in the air.
Yu Yuan gritted her teeth and persisted with her argument. “Sometimes, he does. Sometimes, when Doctor Ling is thinking, he mimics certain surgical actions.”
“Such large movements? He may end up getting the patient infected.”
As he said that, they saw Ling Ran asking the nurse to take off his scrubs before he turned around and washed his hands.
There were always a few doctors who found that annoying. This time, they grabbed the chance and immediately vented their emotions.
“He sure went straight to the point, huh?”
“Is he looking for reinforcements?”
“He’s probably going to read through some books...”
They were quite happy chatting with each other.
As they talked, they saw the door of the operating theater open, and Ling Ran reappeared in the operating theater.
“Focus,” Ling Ran reminded his assistants before he took up the scalpel and pushed it into the patient.
“Bleeding control in the wounded area.” Ling Ran threw a resected liver tissue into a kidney dish.
The visitation room instantly became quiet.
“He cut it just like that?”
“Is that real or my eyes deceiving me?”
“He’s as agile as a rabbit...”
“Aww, I feel like eating a rabbit’s head now.”

However, for the patient, if the doctor had this trick and decided not to use it, the doctor would be considered to be trampling on the patient’s life.
Ling Ran looked slightly dazed.
After all, his attention was on the Virtual Human now.
The doctors in the visitation room turned from feeling calm to feeling puzzled, and they started discussing among themselves.
“Did something go wrong?”
“No matter how I look at it, it was progressing smoothly.”
“Where is the problem?”
Everyone’s proactiveness was awakened.
They paid full attention to the surgery and observed it while they recalled the process of the surgery.
If they could catch Ling Ran’s mistake, their fame would definitely increase.
Yu Yuan pursed her lips in contempt.
She stood straight and said, “Doctor Ling has a habit when he performs surgery.
He often descends into a state where he thinks for a long time.
“It’s just like a Go player.
When you play to the point where it’s time to decide the victor, you need to consider information from different perspectives before making a comprehensive judgment.
While you’re thinking at this moment, you might already be considering his next thirty to forty steps.
“Doctor Ling is also like this.”
The doctors in the visitation room were immediately no longer puzzled.
When Yu Yuan saw this, she raised her head and described the situation to them.
She said, “Doctor Ling’s thinking period varies.
The shortest is about a dozen seconds, and if it’s long, it can last for a few minutes.
When we were in Beijing performing surgery for a patient, Doctor Ling thought for two minutes.
The doctor from Beijing who worked with us thought that Doctor Ling had been intimidated, so he walked away to wash his hands.
But in the end, once Doctor Ling finished thinking, he finished the surgery in just a short while.
The doctor who washed his hands came back in time to help clean up the operating theater.
Hahaha!”
Yu Yuan’s laughter was obviously louder than her height, and her laughter was easily recognizable, causing a few doctors to laugh with her, because it would be embarrassing if they did not.
“So, standing aside to daydream and practice Tai Chi during the middle of surgery is also a habit of Doctor Ling’s?” a doctor standing at the back row took the opportunity to ask during the chaos.
Yu Yuan subconsciously looked at the lower floor.
Indeed, Ling Ran had taken a few steps back while he moved hands in the air.
Yu Yuan gritted her teeth and persisted with her argument.
“Sometimes, he does.
Sometimes, when Doctor Ling is thinking, he mimics certain surgical actions.”
“Such large movements?
He may end up getting the patient infected.”
As he said that, they saw Ling Ran asking the nurse to take off his scrubs before he turned around and washed his hands.
There were always a few doctors who found that annoying.
This time, they grabbed the chance and immediately vented their emotions.
“He sure went straight to the point, huh?”
“Is he looking for reinforcements?”
“He’s probably going to read through some books...”
They were quite happy chatting with each other.
As they talked, they saw the door of the operating theater open, and Ling Ran reappeared in the operating theater.
“Focus,” Ling Ran reminded his assistants before he took up the scalpel and pushed it into the patient.
“Bleeding control in the wounded area.” Ling Ran threw a resected liver tissue into a kidney dish.
The visitation room instantly became quiet.
“He cut it just like that?”
“Is that real or my eyes deceiving me?”
“He’s as agile as a rabbit...”
“Aww, I feel like eating a rabbit’s head now.”

chapters.title: Chapter 919: Explain
paragraphs: When Ling Ran came back to the operating table, he became even more skillful and was at ease with his actions. In more hyperbolic terms, one could say that he had assistance from God.
That was just like how a handsome good student would go to the toilet during his exam and revise his cheat sheet while he was inside. It was as if he received help from God!
He did not only do it fast and well, but also had an imposing air, giving him the feeling that he was going to be absolutely successful.

Many general doctors who were watching the stream, especially the doctors who never touched the liver before, always liked to discuss things based on their experiences of dealing with appendixes or gallbladders. They only felt that Ling Ran was performing quite quickly and smoothly, and they thought that they could perform faster and smoother...
However, when Ling Ran emitted this kind of imposing air ensuring certain victory, these normal doctors instantly felt weak.

What did it mean to have an imposing air guaranteeing certain victory? It meant that the surgeon would not shift from his position once he chose it, and he would not hesitate when he cut into the patient.
This was easier said than done.
Many people could not even do this when cutting a cake, not to mention cutting a human body.

They were like the students who did not bring their cheat sheets yet did not know how to answer the questions. There was confusion in their eyes, and they seized every second they could to make a die from their eraser, then threw it in frenzy to choose an answer from multiple-choice questions to save up time which would allow them to check their answers a second time.
For people who truly knew how to perform the surgery, such as the department director of the General Surgery Department, their expressions would be more serious, and they would speak less.

The anatomical structure of the liver and related parts were very complex. The blood vessels, bile duct, and nerves were like complex cables buried under the tiles in a room. Once the tiles were removed and the cement was overturned, touching even one cable would mean affecting all the other cables.
If those cables were severed, it would be even more troublesome. While they could repair what was in front of them, it was impossible for them to switch out most of the severed cables.

During general surgeries, doctors who could not find the vermiform appendix would definitely face a lot of questions during a liver surgery, such as “What’s this?”, “What’s that?”, “Where’s the part?”, and “Who am I?”
A doctor who could accurately distinguish the paths were rare, while the doctors who could answer everything could be considered first-class doctors.
Meanwhile, a doctor who could perform a surgery at a stable speed was often seen in simple surgeries, but it was rare in complex surgeries.

Ling Ran’s current speed was not slow, but he could retain the same smooth flow in his surgery when he performed both the simple and complex parts of the surgery. This was something that was difficult to accept for people.

“Your Ling Ran has really become experienced with hepatectomy,” the department director of the General Surgery Department could not help but compliment. “He must have performed more than one thousand hepatectomies, right?”

“He has exceeded that number since a long time ago.” Huo Congjun was very satisfied when the department director of the General Surgery Department mentioned that Ling Ran belonged to his department, so his expression turned friendly. “Speaking of which, we should hold a seminar for Ling Ran, and it should be about the one thousand cases of hepatectomy he did so that we can study about hepatectomy. It should be quite good.”
The department director of the General Surgery Department laughed. “Of course it’ll be good if you’re willing to make it.”
Holding a seminar was very easy, but the problem was money and manpower.
And people generally did not like to participate in a low-level seminar, as it did not bring any meaning.
However, for a young doctor like Ling Ran, any seminar in which he was the main character was precious. Other hospitals would never offer such a chance to their young doctors.
When that thought came to Huo Congjun’s mind, he started to think about the details.
The Emergency Medical Centre had a lot of money.

“Doctor Ling has now started to perform a resection for another area with metastasis.” Yu Yuan stood slightly close to the front while she introduced the progress of the surgery loudly. Since the doctors watching the live stream could not see her, they thought that she was just like a radio announcer, which caused her to be even more believable.

“As of current, he is still performing the ligation of blood vessels. In the past, Doctor Ling’s greatest strength was anastomosis. Now, he can also perform the operations on blood vessels very quickly. Besides, Doctor Ling’s understanding of the blood vessels’ anatomical structure surpasses that of normal people.” Yu Yuan stopped for a while and said, “This is especially so after his long thinking sessions. After those sessions, the details in Doctor Ling’s surgeries will always be performed incredibly well.”
Everyone looked at Yu Yuan like she was joking, but most of them already felt defeated.

Yu Yuan’s voice continued to drift about the visitation room. “You can currently see that Doctor Ling just avoided a small blood vessel... Hmm, this is a common situation when Doctor Ling performs surgery. Just like what I’ve said. Doctor Ling’s judgment toward the position of the blood vessels is sometimes very precise, in fact, it is extraordinarily precise.”
“It’s as if he just cheated,” said one young doctor very suddenly.

When somebody said that, another person immediately said, “I heard that the United States has developed an imaging technique that can show the position of blood vessels. It’s almost the same as coronary angiography. The safety is even higher...”
“Can you remember it, though?” That question was sprayed on the doctor’s face like an icy shower.
The doctor was instantly rendered speechless.

Forget about the fact that the positions of blood vessels was different in every individual, most of the people still did not know how to perform lymphadenectomy even if the lymphatic vessels were divided into such obvious regions.
“Now that I think about it, how did Ling Ran do that?” This time, the question was passed to Yu Yuan.
Everyone was here to watch the surgery, and they obviously had a goal in mind. Their most basic purpose of being there was to know whether they could do it.
Before Yu Yuan spoke, another female doctor in the room said airily, “Does Doctor Ling only cheat during operations?”

Everyone placed their attention on the operating theater. On the opposite side of the glass were shadowless lights, masks, and surgical caps, but even with those things, they still felt as if Ling Ran had cheated, somehow.
“Some people can cheat in a test whenever they want, while some will still be unfortunate whether they cheat or not.” An empathic sigh made the atmosphere in the visitation room plunge to the bottom.
Meanwhile, the atmosphere in the operating theater became better.
After receiving more knowledge through the Virtual Human halfway through the surgery, Ling Ran’s surgery became smoother.
To his current self, he was already very familiar with being able to perform surgeries smoothly, and it was especially so for surgeries like hepatectomy. Ling Ran could handle it with ease.
However, Young Dai’s body condition was too bad, and his abdominal cavity was a mess. Ling Ran was not very confident about whether he could go through with the entire radical surgery either.
In fact, he had the thought of turning it into a palliative surgery.
If he went through a palliative surgery, the patient might die soon. He could live for a few months only, but he could at least say goodbye to his family and friends when he was still conscious.

Radical surgery was what Ling Ran pursued. If he did not want to challenge the possibility of radical surgery, he would not have arranged surgery for the patient. After all, the completion of a radical surgery also did not mean a longer survival period.
Everything relied on probability.

However, the probability of surviving in radical surgery was always higher. Besides, the possibility of complete recovery also existed. Although this possibility was extremely low, this kind of probable existence could still produce a qualitative change in the patient.
However, the requirement of radical surgery was very strict, so much so that even at the last moment of the Ling Ran, Ling Ran was still not certain whether the surgery was successful or not.
‘I’ll definitely succeed,’ Ling Ran thought. He then raised his head slightly. “Wipe off my sweat.”
A nurse quickly wiped off the sweat from his forehead, and Ling Ran was seen throwing himself into the surgery again.

chapters.title: Chapter 920: Slow
paragraphs: In the records within the Changxi Province, the average time for combined liver and pancreatic radical surgery was more than six hours.
Ling Ran did it slower, though.
Over the past half a year, Ling Ran’s average surgery time had increased greatly.

When Ling Ran only had Master Level Hepatectomy skill, the average time of each hepatectomy usually required three hours. If he was fast and the patient’s condition was ideal for surgery, he would usually finish removing the liver in one hour.
After Ling Ran obtained Perfect Level Tissue Separation and as he continued upgrading himself until he obtained Perfect Level Hepatectomy, his surgery time started slowing down at a consistent pace.
That was because the more skills he learned and mastered, the more attention into the details he needed to place. In order to handle the details well, he needed more time.

Take small vessels as an example. Some needed to be cut with an endotherm knife, some needed to be bypassed and kept, some needed to be cut or sutured, and it all depended on how Ling Ran handled them.
In such surgery, only very few doctors could make their selection freely.

Combined liver and pancreatic radical surgery required two different doctors working together and performing the surgery accordingly. It would be impossible to say that no mistake would be made. It would be very rare if the surgery could be performed without any major mistakes, even if they continued making minor mistakes, and the remaining part would depend on the patient.

If this were put in comparison with the difficulty in building a house, the difficulty of subtotal gastrectomy was like a man building a tile-roofed house. For those who cared about the details would talk about the windows and the tiles, and for those who did not care, they would just simply build a tile-roofed house shaped like a matchbox.

Hepatectomy was at the level of building a two-story or three-story building. No matter how crude the work was, they would still need to adhere to the canon. For those who wanted to do a better job, they would set their standards very high. It would not be strange for them to come up with something that would let them win designing rewards.
Combined hepatectomy and gastrectomy were like building many houses. Many would not even be able to meet the lowest expectations, much less the highest expectations.
Very few doctors could finish observing an entire gastrectomy in combination with hepatic resection.
It took too much time. Furthermore, the excitement was gone after observing for too long, and the surgery would be boring.
However, for doctors like the department director of the General Surgery Department, the further he watched, the more interesting he felt the surgery was.
The doctors in the visitation room had come in and left, but the number of people remained the same. Only when there were fewer people in the room would Yu Yuan be seen.

At that moment, Yu Yuan would raise her chin proudly and give a brief description of the surgery for the doctors who just came in. She was like a dwarf wolf within a pack of wolves and lecturing newcomers.

“Based on current literature, positive intravascular cancer embolus, positive lymphoma, serosal invasion, retroperitoneal metastasis, and the timing of liver metastasis are high-risk factors that will affect the prognosis of liver metastasis...

“Some follow-ups for liver cancer metastasis show that the median survival rate for patients who undergo surgical treatment only survive for eighteen to twenty months. However, once they survive for more than twenty months, the survival rate will increase tremendously...
“When the area of the liver metastasis is more than 1.57 inches, it will have a greater effect on the surgery and the prognosis. Yes, Doctor Ling has basically finished operating on the liver...”

Yu Yuan kept talking about the surgery, but no one was annoyed by her. Then, she started talking about research papers and the situations of the patients in the research papers, and these were things that even department directors might not know.

The refinement of modern medicine resulted in many doctors who could only specialize in their respective areas. If the surgeries were not frequently performed, did not involve the skills they learned or were not famous surgery plans, normal doctors would not read the related research papers carefully.
Everyone’s time was very precious. After all, normal people still needed to sleep at night.

Right then, all the doctors felt good as they observed the surgery while listening to the general introduction given by Yu Yuan. They felt that it was worth it to come over, and they did not waste their time.
When dinner time arrived, crispy bread was served, and the authentic flavor of wheat deepened everyone’s memory of the surgery.

“Everyone, you must be tired. This was prepared by our own chef from Yunli Medical Company. Feel free to take one or two and give us some comments if you’re free.” Mai Chun entered the visitation room the same way she always did. She first smiled without saying anything and immediately displayed the characteristics of a pharmaceutical sales representative.
Some doctors smiled while they ate the bread, some ate the bread with a serious look, and some frowned while they ate the bread...
Mai Chun was used to the attitude of the doctors. She still put on a smile on her face but pouted in secret while she said in her mind, ‘If you don’t want it, then don’t eat it!’
Huo Congjun pressed the call button and asked, “Ling Ran, do you want to rest for a while and eat something first?”
“No need. I’ll finish very soon,” Ling Ran replied firmly, and his hands did not stop moving at all.
“Oh... Hmm? Are you finishing soon?” Huo Congjun replied and found that something was off.
“I need... around an hour or so.” The time given by Ling Ran was obviously different from what others would usually consider “soon”.
Huo Congjun burst into laughter. He nodded, pressed the button, and said, “Just go along at your own pace.”
Huo Congjun did not even care whether the other assistants could eat anything or whether they were hungry.
Doctors were the most unhealthy group in the world. They did not eat accordingly, and it was also normal for them to overeat.

The department director of the General Surgery Department did not care about the assistants as well. He smiled and pointed at Yu Yuan before he said, “You can continue to talk as entertainment. Old Huo, the Emergency Medical Center has recruited many new talents, huh?”
“Doctor Yu cannot be counted as a newbie anymore.” Huo Congjun smiled. “Once she finishes her training as a chief resident, she should be promoted to an attending physician.”
The department director of the General Surgery Department hummed in reply, and the doctors at the side chuckled before they said, “You’re saying that’s not a newbie?”
The doctors in the visitation room had changed twice. Ling Ran started to finish up the surgery when it was nearing evening.
At this moment, his assistants had changed once.

However, due to the surgery difficulty and the ability of the assistants, today’s surgery only allowed the first and second assistant to be replaced by the third and fourth assistant. So, when the surgery ended, everyone was so hungry that their eyes were bloodshot.
“Quick, go and get some food.”
“Is there anything to eat?”
“Pork trotters? Are there any pork trotters?”
The assistants went out of the operating theater and went to the waiting room with the fastest speed they could muster. Their legs were numb and their eyes were bloodshot because of their hunger.
Those people schooled their expressions and bared their teeth. Their bloodshot eyes shone with the light of those longing for food.
The young chef in the waiting room stared at them and hesitantly said, “Aren’t you guys performing surgery?”
“Nonsense, where are the pork trotters? Where is my braised meat?” Lu Wenbin asked while he looked around in the kitchen.

The young chef held the handle of the frying pan quietly and said coldly, “Old Lu, let me ask you something. You can answer after you think about it. Did all of you get infected by something during the surgery?”
